function validate_fit(d, c, f, mapped)
    failures = String[]
    require_check!(failures, finite_fit(f), "nonfinite_return")
    require_check!(failures, f.traits == d.traits[c.permutation], "fit_trait_labels")
    require_check!(failures, f.breeding_values.traits == d.traits[c.permutation], "EBV_trait_labels")
    require_check!(failures, f.breeding_values.ids == d.ids, "EBV_ID_order")
    require_check!(failures, f.genetic_structure == :factor_analytic && f.genetic_rank == 1,
                   "FA_structure_rank")
    require_check!(failures, isapprox(f.genetic_covariance,
        f.genetic_loadings * transpose(f.genetic_loadings) + Diagonal(f.genetic_uniqueness);
        rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-10), "G_reconstruction")
    require_check!(failures, isapprox(mapped.G,
        mapped.loadings * transpose(mapped.loadings) + Diagonal(mapped.psi);
        rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-10), "mapped_G_reconstruction")
    require_check!(failures, all(>=(FLOOR), f.genetic_uniqueness), "returned_psi_below_floor")
    direct = fixed_eval(d, d.Y * c.M, f.genetic_covariance, f.residual_covariance)
    require_check!(failures, abs(f.loglik - direct.loglik) <= ORACLE_ATOL, "returned_loglik_reevaluation")
    require_check!(failures, isapprox(f.beta, direct.beta; rtol = SOLVE_RTOL, atol = SOLVE_ATOL),
                   "returned_beta_reevaluation")
    require_check!(failures, isapprox(f.breeding_values.values, direct.ebv;
        rtol = SOLVE_RTOL, atol = SOLVE_ATOL), "returned_EBV_reevaluation")
    dg = f.fa_start_diagnostics
    require_check!(failures, dg.strategy == :default_and_balanced && dg.starts_attempted == 2 &&
        length(dg.starts) == 2 && [s.name for s in dg.starts] == [:default, :balanced],
        "ordinary_two_start_status")
    valid = filter(s -> s.valid && s.loglik !== nothing && isfinite(s.loglik), collect(dg.starts))
    converged = filter(s -> s.converged, valid)
    eligible = isempty(converged) ? valid : converged
    if isempty(eligible)
        push!(failures, "no_valid_reported_start")
    else
        chosen = eligible[argmax([s.loglik for s in eligible])]
        require_check!(failures, chosen.name == dg.selected_start && chosen.converged == f.converged &&
            chosen.iterations == f.iterations && abs(chosen.loglik - f.loglik) <= ORACLE_ATOL,
            "selected_start_status")
        better = any(s -> !s.converged && s.loglik > chosen.loglik, valid)
        require_check!(failures, dg.better_nonconverged_start == better, "better_nonconverged_status")
        expected_range = length(valid) > 1 ? maximum(s.loglik for s in valid) - minimum(s.loglik for s in valid) : nothing
        require_check!(failures, expected_range === nothing ? dg.objective_range === nothing :
            isapprox(dg.objective_range, expected_range; atol = 1e-8, rtol = 1e-10), "objective_range_status")
    end
    distance = minimum(f.genetic_uniqueness .- FLOOR)
    require_check!(failures, isapprox(dg.minimum_uniqueness, minimum(f.genetic_uniqueness);
        atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-12) && isapprox(dg.uniqueness_floor_distance, distance;
        atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-12), "uniqueness_status")
    require_check!(failures, dg.near_uniqueness_floor == (distance <= 0.01 * FLOOR), "near_floor_status")
    (; failures, direct)
end

module ValidationDebtTracker

# Validation-debt burn-down tracker. CONSUMES the live `validation_status()` rows
# (id/capability/phase/status/evidence/missing/claim_boundary) and reports status
# counts, a per-phase breakdown, and the verbatim open-debt list. Reporting only —
# reads existing `ValidationStatusRow.status`/`.missing`; it fits nothing, runs no
# comparator, and promotes no capability. Mirrors the unexported, dependency-light
# `sim/summarize_recovery_calibration.jl` pattern (not exported from the package).

using HSquared

export status_counts, phase_status_counts, open_debts, markdown_summary

const _ORDER = ["covered", "covered_external", "partial", "planned"]

"""Counts by status in the fixed maturity order; each bucket emitted once even if zero."""
function status_counts(status = validation_status())
    counts = Dict{String,Int}()
    for row in status
        counts[row.status] = get(counts, row.status, 0) + 1
    end
    return [s => get(counts, s, 0) for s in _ORDER]
end

"""phase => status => count."""
function phase_status_counts(status = validation_status())
    out = Dict{String,Dict{String,Int}}()
    for row in status
        d = get!(out, row.phase, Dict{String,Int}())
        d[row.status] = get(d, row.status, 0) + 1
    end
    return out
end

"""Every non-covered row (covered_external included — those rows keep open `missing` debts),
in `validation_status()` order, with the `missing` text verbatim."""
function open_debts(status = validation_status())
    rows = NamedTuple{(:id, :capability, :phase, :status, :missing),
                      Tuple{String,String,String,String,String}}[]
    for row in status
        row.status == "covered" && continue
        push!(rows, (id = row.id, capability = row.capability, phase = row.phase,
                     status = row.status, missing = row.missing))
    end
    return rows
end

# sort phases as Phase 0 < Phase 1 < ... < Phase 4B < ... < non-"Phase" last, stable by text
function _phase_key(p)
    m = match(r"^Phase (\d+)", p)
    return m === nothing ? (99, 0, p) : (parse(Int, m.captures[1]),
                                         occursin(r"^Phase \d+[A-Za-z]", p) ? 1 : 0, p)
end

"""Deterministic burn-down markdown: status table, per-phase table, open-debt list."""
function markdown_summary(status = validation_status())
    lines = String["# Validation-Debt Burn-Down", ""]
    push!(lines, "| status | rows |")
    push!(lines, "| --- | ---: |")
    total = 0
    for (s, n) in status_counts(status)
        push!(lines, "| $s | $n |")
        total += n
    end
    push!(lines, "| **total** | $total |")
    push!(lines, "", "## Per phase", "")
    push!(lines, "| phase | covered | covered_external | partial | planned | total |")
    push!(lines, "| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |")
    psc = phase_status_counts(status)
    for phase in sort(collect(keys(psc)); by = _phase_key)
        d = psc[phase]
        c = get(d, "covered", 0); ce = get(d, "covered_external", 0)
        pa = get(d, "partial", 0); pl = get(d, "planned", 0)
        push!(lines, "| $phase | $c | $ce | $pa | $pl | $(c + ce + pa + pl) |")
    end
    push!(lines, "", "## Open debts", "")
    for d in open_debts(status)
        push!(lines, "- $(d.id) ($(d.status), $(d.phase)) — $(d.capability): $(d.missing)")
    end
    return join(lines, "\n")

function write_validation_status_table!(
    page_path::AbstractString = joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "docs", "src", "validation-status.md");
    status = validation_status(),
)
    page = read(page_path, String)
    occursin(BEGIN_MARK, page) || error("missing begin marker in $page_path")
    occursin(END_MARK, page) || error("missing end marker in $page_path")

    table = validation_status_table_markdown(status)
    block = string(BEGIN_MARK, "\n\n", table, "\n", END_MARK)
    i0 = findfirst(BEGIN_MARK, page)
    i1 = findfirst(END_MARK, page)
    (i0 === nothing || i1 === nothing) && error("markers not found in $page_path")
    i1.start > i0.start || error("end marker precedes begin marker in $page_path")
    updated = string(page[1:(i0.start - 1)], block, page[(i1.stop + 1):end])
    write(page_path, updated)
    return page_path
end

# Bounded automatic genetic FA-rank contract

Status: design frozen for future implementation review, 2026-10-01. No automatic selector is implemented or validated by this document. The current fixed-rank Gaussian FA route remains experimental, and public covered count stays seven. Approved scope and execution record: [design arc](auto-fa-rank-design-plan-20261001.md).

## Model and candidates

The first selector is explicit opt-in and compares only shared genetic factor counts `K={0,1}` for four complete Gaussian traits, pedigree relationships, one record per observed animal, trait intercepts and an unstructured residual covariance. The same records, labels, units, X, Z and Ainv are used for both candidates. Explicit fixed-rank calls keep their current meaning; omission of rank does not invoke selection. Missing responses, other trait counts/ranks, other fixed effects, genomic/custom relationships, repeatability and non-Gaussian models are refused before fitting. K=2 is outside this design.

Write `Y=XB+ZU+E`. For the engine's record-major order, `y=vec(Y')`, `u=vec(U')`, `X_full=X⊗I_4`, `Z_full=Z⊗I_4`,

`Cov(u)=A⊗G_K`, `Cov(vec(E'))=I_n⊗R`,

`V_K=Z_full(A⊗G_K)Z_full'+I_n⊗R`,

`G_K=L_K L_K'+diag(psi)`, `psi_i=c+exp(theta_i)`, `c=1e-4` in squared units of trait i.

| Candidate | Shape and future implementation mapping | Genetic parameters |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| K=0 | Diagonal G with positive trait-specific genetic variances. Selector-internal floor-matched diagonal fit; no loading columns. | 4 |
| K=1 | Existing FA shape with four loadings and four positive uniquenesses; rank-one shared component. | 8 |

K measures shared factors, not the rank of G, which is positive definite when uniquenesses are positive. K=0 still permits genetic variance. Zero genetic signal is a separate boundary case, outside the fitted strictly-positive family.

The existing public diagonal route uses `exp(theta)` without c, while FA uses `c+exp(theta)`. A direct call to the current diagonal fitter is therefore not a floor-matched nested comparator. Future implementation must add the matched internal candidate without changing the public fixed-rank diagonal route, the FA rank guard or the existing floor. It must retain ten identical residual log-Cholesky coordinates in both candidates. Exact source findings: [engine review](../dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/engine-contract.md), `src/multivariate.jl:660-723,844-856,1010-1055` at base `28f90e09`.

Identifiability is a property of the covariance and record design. With one record per animal, Z=I and A=I, only G+R is identifiable. That design is refused for automatic selection; its likelihood is retained as a deterministic negative witness. The identification screen must compare genetic and residual kernels on the REML contrast space: use Q with Q'X_full=0 and inspect Q'V_K Q, not raw A versus I alone. Exact or numerically unresolved proportional kernels on that space must refuse selection with a design-identification reason. For intercept-only one-record data, the informative-looking half-sib matrix A=(1-rho)I+rho*11' becomes (1-rho)I after removing the intercept direction; G and R remain confounded. This is a second deterministic refusal witness. Relatedness alone does not establish good finite-sample information. The future pre-run must freeze a numerical kernel-rank check and its unit convention before real selection fits; no numerical conditioning threshold is claimed validated here.

For general K the nominal genetic dimension is `4K-K(K-1)/2+4`. At K=2 it exceeds the ten-dimensional ambient symmetric G space. This dimension screen does not prove identifiability at K=1. At L=0 the derivative of LL' is zero; diagonal-to-FA nesting is singular, so the score below is not a regular four-df likelihood-ratio test.

## Criterion and numerical comparison

Freeze criterion name `reml_aic_covariance` as an experimental comparison rule on the common fixed-effect contrast space:

`C_K=-2*ell_REML,K+2*q_K`, `q_K=q_G(K)+q_R`, `q_R=10`.

The exact engine REML normalization is

`ell_REML=-0.5*((4n-p_full)*log(2*pi)+logdet(V)+logdet(X_full' V^-1 X_full)+y'P y)`,

`P=V^-1-V^-1 X_full (X_full'V^-1 X_full)^-1 X_full'V^-1`, `p_full=4`.

The four common fixed intercepts are removed by REML and not counted in q. The displayed q values are 14 and 18; penalties are 28 and 36. Counting common intercepts in both penalties would shift scores equally but is not this declared convention. Residual parameters are counted and displayed even though they cancel in the difference.

Define signed difference `D=C_1-C_0=8-2*(ell_1-ell_0)`. Negative D favors K=1. Away from numerical ties, K=1 wins when `2*(ell_1-ell_0)>8`. Report both full C values and D; calculate D directly from the likelihood difference to reduce cancellation. Reevaluate both objectives on the identical input model before ranking.

Freeze numerical tie band `tau=1e-6` criterion units for the initial moderate-scale validation cell. Require each returned loglik to agree with independent same-covariance reevaluation within `1e-8` absolute loglik units before selection. Thus the two objective discrepancies can contribute at most `4e-8` to D under this check, below tau; this discrepancy budget is a check convention, not a proof of all floating-point or optimizer error. If the future pre-run cannot meet it, stop and revise the numerical contract before any campaign. Do not enlarge it after seeing selected ranks.

If `abs(D)<=tau`, choose K=0 and set `near_tie=true`; an exact tie is included. If D is below -tau choose K=1; otherwise choose K=0. Return tau and the objective discrepancies. This band handles numerical ambiguity; it is not an evidence-strength cutoff or a calibrated confidence interval. Weak substantive separation remains visible as the raw D, even when outside tau.

This is a restricted-likelihood covariance comparison with nominal parameter penalties and a singular smaller model. It does not establish consistency, correct biological dimension, marginal predictive optimality or calibrated rank probabilities. Gurka discusses ambiguities in REML model selection; the chosen bounded rule needs its own selection study. [Gurka (2006)](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1198/000313006X90396).

The mixed-model selection review motivates keeping the likelihood target, covariance boundaries and effective sample size explicit. [Müller, Scealy and Welsh (2013)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.2427). BIC is deferred because no pedigree-specific effective sample-size rule has been justified. [Delattre, Lavielle and Poursat (2014)](https://doi.org/10.1214/14-EJS890). The singular boundary also prevents treating D as an ordinary chi-square test. [Self and Liang (1987)](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1987.10478472). These sources motivate limits; none validates this exact selector.

Marginal ML-AIC would require a genuinely fitted ML objective for both candidates. Evaluating ML only at REML estimates is excluded. Conditional AIC, BIC, rank probabilities and automatic criterion switching are outside this first contract.

## Starts, eligibility and failure policy

Fit the floor-matched diagonal candidate from the documented phenotype-based default; fit FA from its existing default and balanced starts. Neither uses generating truth. Permit at most one additional FA retry, only when the initial FA candidate is failed, unconverged or materially non-nested relative to the eligible diagonal candidate, or when a better finite unconverged FA attempt exceeds the best eligible converged FA loglik by more than tau/2. Thus the first budget is one diagonal optimizer start and at most three FA starts, four total. The unequal budget is declared; it does not imply equal optimization robustness.

The additional FA start uses the diagonal covariance as a target with a deterministic, nonzero loading perturbation and corresponding floor-safe uniquenesses, preserving the covariance as closely as feasible. The implementation must write the exact initializer and verify it before fitting. A zero-loading start is excluded because its first-order loading gradient vanishes. No extra retries, changed data, changed floor or hidden warm starts are allowed. Retain the initial attempt even if the retry succeeds.

Each candidate uses its best eligible converged start within this budget. Eligibility requires finite objective and estimates, positive-definite G and R, the shared floor constraint, convergence, matched inputs/normalization and successful objective reevaluation. A better finite unconverged start exceeding the chosen converged loglik by `tau/2` makes selection unavailable after the one allowed retry. Start covariance disagreement and objective ranges remain visible; they do not certify a global optimum.

With a matched floor, the FA family contains the diagonal covariance at L=0. If the best eligible FA loglik remains below the diagonal loglik by more than `tau/2`, flag a nesting/optimization failure and refuse selection. The nested witness is an objective evaluation at L=0, not a successful FA optimization claim.

All tau/2 comparisons above use loglik units because tau is defined in criterion units. Both candidate ranks must be eligible to select a rank. If either fails after its budget, return `selection_status=unavailable`, no selected rank/fit, a reason and all attempts. A sole successful candidate does not win by default. The user may request an explicit fixed rank independently; no silent fallback fit is made.

Near-floor candidates can remain eligible under the experimental score, with `boundary_sensitive=true`. The floor flag is defined for both candidates because both now share c. It is not a claim of uniqueness identification. At or numerically below the bound is an admissibility failure. The fixed absolute floor is unit-dependent; no silent standardization, rescaling or new preprocessing is introduced. Unit-change validation must identify where selection changes because constraints change.

| requested_ranks, selected_rank | Always requested {0,1}; selected integer or missing. |
| criterion, criterion_status, q, penalties | reml_aic_covariance, experimental; per-candidate counts and scores. |
| criterion_difference, tie_tolerance, near_tie | D=C1-C0, tau and numerical tie flag. |
| records/design/relationship fingerprint | Demonstrate identical model inputs across candidates. |
| candidate_summary | One row per requested rank, including unattempted/failed ranks and eligibility reason. |
| attempts | One row per start/retry, preserving failures and diagnostic fields. |
| boundary_sensitive, start_sensitive | Visible flags derived from retained fits and attempts. |
| uncertainty_scope | conditional_on_selected_rank; no selection-adjusted uncertainty claim. |

Each attempt row records rank, structure, start ID, retry index, attempted status, failure reason, converged, optimizer status/iterations, finite-value/PD checks, returned and reevaluated loglik, q/criterion when defined, per-trait uniqueness and floor distances, near-floor flags, eligibility and selected marker. Failed values are missing with reasons, never zero. The candidate summary separates the chosen within-rank start from the selected rank.

The candidate_summary is the authoritative retained row for every requested rank, including preflight-unattempted ranks. The attempts table contains actual starts only; no synthetic optimizer-start rows are created for unattempted ranks. Preflight refusals mark both candidate-summary rows unattempted with the reason. Interrupts abort promptly and propagate cancellation; the future wrapper/harness must retain its partial attempt ledger and mark interrupted/unattempted rows without pretending to return a completed selection. The interruption mechanism is an implementation acceptance item, not permission to swallow an interrupt.

Proposed function name `select_fa_rank` is reserved for design discussion. It is not an implemented export or approved R grammar. Any future R expert-control payload must preserve the full table, missing reasons, scores, flags and selected covariance/EBVs in original label order. The existing bounded R fixed-rank transport is verified at immutable R merge `e82f5c95`; automatic-selection fields are new work. [User-contract review](../dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/user-contract.md).

Suggested summary: “This rule preferred zero shared genetic factors (diagonal genetic covariance) / one shared genetic factor among the two eligible candidates. The attempt table shows the comparison and any boundary or start sensitivity. Uncertainty from the fitted model is conditional on this chosen rank.” Avoid describing K as the true number of biological dimensions.

## Freeze and remaining implementation obligations

The candidate set, model shape, experimental score/parameter convention, signed difference, tie rule, strict two-candidate eligibility, retry ceiling and returned semantics are frozen for this bounded implementation proposal. The numerical acceptance tolerances above are predeclared engineering checks, not measured successes.

The internal diagonal floor, actual retry initializer, numerical kernel-identification screen and interruption transport must be implemented and independently checked before running selection fits. They are specified acceptance obligations with clear failure outcomes, not current capabilities. Broader statistical selection performance, defaults and public promotion require the separate validation plan. No source/test, capability, validation-debt or release change is made here.
# Automatic genetic FA-rank validation plan

Status: predeclared plan for later implementation and validation, 2026-10-01. This design arc executes no fits, simulations, benchmark or campaign. [Contract](auto-fa-rank-contract.md) defines the proposed T4 complete-response pedigree Gaussian comparison. The frozen fixed-rank 200-seed campaign remains untouched.

## Acceptance ladder

| Stage | Evidence required | Honest completion statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V0 design | Independent model/user/claim review; criterion, failures and limits explicit. | Design ready for a bounded implementation proposal. |
| V1 deterministic implementation | Independent dense objective and penalty references, comparator shape/floor, policy/refusal/interrupt tests, source review and fixed-rank compatibility. | Selector mechanics implemented at the tested cell. |
| V2 pre-run | Non-empty ordinary-start results, readable attempt tables, expected engineered witnesses and measured cost. | Ready to size a separate diagnostic study. |
| V3 diagnostic study | Frozen scenarios, truth, seeds, denominators and outputs; all attempts retained. | Measured selection behavior for the declared cells. |
| V4 twin integration | Same-input R/Julia fixtures, serialized complete ledger, exact-current tests/docs and independent audit. | Bounded experimental expert route integrated. |

No rung automatically changes covered count or public defaults. Public activation or a reliability/calibration claim requires its own stated evidence and owner-approved scope. A mechanically correct selector can still choose poorly under weak signals.

## Deterministic tests and tests of the tests

| ID | Independent oracle or controlled witness | Required outcome / negative control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| O1 shape/floor | Direct G=LL'+diag(psi); K0 psi=c+exp(theta), K1 same c. | qG=4/8, qR=10; fixed public diagonal remains exp(theta). Deliberately unmatched floor must fail comparator conformance. |
| O2 vector/order | Record-major Kronecker covariance constructed independently in base R and Julia. | Input labels and V agree; trait/animal permutation mapped back. Deliberate order swap must fail. |
| O3 objective | Dense Cholesky GLS and explicit REML formula, independent of selector helper. Evaluate identical returned G/R, not a truth-start optimum. | Returned loglik discrepancy <=1e-8 for each moderate-scale witness; altered normalisation or fixed design must fail. |
| O4 penalty/score | Hand-calculated q={14,18}, C={-2ell0+28,-2ell1+36}, D=8-2deltaell. | Algebra/sign match. A wrong penalty or sign must change the manufactured winner and be detected. |
| O5 ties | Manufactured ell differences below, exactly at and above 4, including score offsets just inside/outside tau=1e-6. | Exact/numerical tie selects0; D below -tau selects1; no loss of either row. Changed tie policy must fail. |
| O6 failure table | Inject nonfinite, nonconverged, non-PD, failed and unattempted outcomes at each rank/start. | Any unavailable rank means unavailable selection; preserve all actual start rows, both candidate-summary rows and reasons. Preflight creates no synthetic start rows. Sole survivor must not silently win. |
| O7 retry/nesting | L=0 objective equals the matched diagonal covariance; manufactured non-monotonic FA result and better-unconverged attempt. | The mixed converged-plus-better-unconverged case must invoke the single allowed FA retry. At most four optimizer starts, then unavailable if unresolved. A zero-gradient L=0 initializer must be refused as the retry start. |
| O8 identifiability | One-record A=I, Z=I gives V=I⊗(G+R); create distinct G/R pairs with same V. Also use half-sibs A=(1-rho)I+rho*11' with trait intercepts: project through Q'X_full=0 and show proportional REML genetic/residual kernels. | Refuse automatic selection and preserve design-identification reason. Screen the projected REML covariance kernels, not raw relatedness; freeze the numerical rank criterion before real fit use. |
| O9 scope/compatibility | Complete T4 pedigree intercept-only route plus each forbidden family/rank/missingness/provider/design. | Clear preflight refusals; original fixed-rank outputs and guards unchanged. |
| O10 interruption | Controlled interruption during each start and between candidates. | Prompt cancellation; partial ledger retained, remaining rows unattempted; never an apparently completed winner. |
| O11 transport | Plain-data serialization fixtures in both twins, including missing criterion/reason fields. | Same selected rank, covariances, score difference, labels, complete table and warnings; no row dropped during data-frame conversion. |

Pure score/policy tests are independent of Julia fitting. Engine integration tests must require the real bridge rather than silently pass after skips. The earlier fixed-covariance base-R reference and FA unit/order harness are scaffolding; their truth-informed optimizer start and fixed-rank scope do not constitute selector recovery evidence. Existing files are cited in the [engine receipt](../dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/engine-contract.md).

A test of the score does not prove the optimizer finds its maximum. Retain within-rank default/balanced attempts and objective/covariance disagreement separately from cross-rank choice.

## Future pre-run, not launched

After a separate implementation approval and V1 pass, propose four ordinary-start datasets on a small informative pedigree: diagonal genetic truth, clear one-factor truth, weak one-factor truth and uniqueness close to the matched floor. Use 50 observed animals initially, four complete traits and one observation per animal. Truth files must specify all pedigree IDs, founders/parents, X/Z, B, L, psi and R; generate genetic effects with A and residual effects independently. Do not center drawn genetic effects or delete their sampling variation.

Pre-run output is one manifest plus full candidate/start rows, selected/unavailable outcome, score difference, covariance error, floor/start flags, objective reevaluation, elapsed time and peak memory per dataset. The first file must be inspected immediately. All failed fits remain visible; blank/NA-only outputs stop the probe. The weak-factor dataset has no promised rank winner; it tests whether the system reports ambiguity rather than whether a noisy selector gets truth right.

Cost is not yet measured for the new selector. Prior fixed-rank full-suite receipts around eight minutes are not a per-dataset runtime estimate. Before launching, use the new implementation's first single dataset with a ten-minute owned timeout to measure fit cost; state this ten-minute cap, one Julia and one BLAS thread, and stop/re-report if it overruns. Only then estimate the remaining three datasets from observed elapsed time and memory. This is a future measurement proposal, not a run authorized by this design arc.

A few bounded fixtures may run locally. Serious replicated recovery belongs on Totoro, capped at 150 cores and normally one Julia/BLAS thread per replicate; DRAC is an alternative if queue/array needs justify it. Never compute on a DRAC login node, trigger Duo or run a campaign on GitHub Actions. For a projected run over three hours, show the pre-run result and complete simulation plan to Shinichi before full execution. No remote run is approved here.

## Proposed later scenario grid

Use informative pedigrees and complete T4 data, with observed-animal sample-size rungs 50,150,400 and a larger easy rung only if the pre-run permits a realistic compute budget. Four truths are primary: diagonal G (shared-factor K0), weak K1, clearly separated K1, and near-floor K1. A separately labelled G=0 witness is deliberate model misspecification because the fitted families require positive uniqueness. Uninformative and weak-information pedigree cases are separate identification/availability cells, not excluded fits that disappear from the denominator.

For every truth/sample-size cell, retain selected0, selected1, unavailable, interruption, timeout, failure mechanism, unattempted cases, criterion margins, eligible fractions, start/floor flags, covariance recovery and runtime/memory. Always report correct-rank fraction over all declared datasets, and separately the conditional fraction among selections. Unavailable counts as not correctly selected in the first fraction. Genetic covariance rank remains four in both strictly positive-uniqueness candidates; report shared-factor count rather than matrix rank.

Run real alternate starts, trait permutations, animal orderings and unit transforms as paired witnesses, not independent extra datasets. Test moderate rescaling away from the floor and deliberate crossing of the absolute floor separately. Equivalent score differences are required for cases whose parameter constraints map bijectively and whose reference objective agrees. A scale change that alters the feasible floor set must be reported as a contract limitation; it cannot be called invariance. No hidden standardization is allowed.

## Before a replicated study

Freeze the exact generating covariance/relationship files, numerical and optimizer controls, retry initializer, seeds, replicate count, sample-size ladder, machine/thread cap, command and observed runtime estimate. Freeze all denominator and failure classes before reading aggregate results. Do not choose a success cutoff after seeing a selection distribution or restart the old fixed-rank campaign.

The first later study is descriptive, with no promised universal correct-rank percentage. Choose replicate count from a prespecified Monte Carlo precision target and measured cost; for example, a worst-case binomial MCSE target of five percentage points requires at least 100 independent datasets per primary cell. This follows sqrt(0.25/m), not a statistical validity claim for the selector. The final grid and budget require a separate pre-run-supported campaign proposal.

Engineering acceptance requires every deterministic policy/reference witness to pass or be explicitly removed from supported scope. Clear-signal easy cells must demonstrate the deciding likelihood improvement against an independent same-model reference before descending to weak/small-sample cells. If they fail, classify simulator, objective, optimizer, criterion or bridge mechanisms before enlarging a study. Empirical rank frequency has no universal acceptance threshold in this design; reported results determine the strength and scope of any later usability claim.

Intervals and standard errors are conditional on selected rank. Coverage across a selected model requires its own predeclared inferential study; this plan supplies no confidence-level or biological-rank probability claim.

## Deliverables and ownership

Implementation proposal: exact narrow source/test changes, new internal floor-matched diagonal route, candidate wrapper/ledger, retry and identification checks, pure score tests and same-data references. It must identify ownership in both twins before editing either.

Diagnostic proposal: retained JSON/CSV truth/attempt manifests, per-cell tables and failed logs, explicit fixed-rank compatibility, source/runtime freeze, independent review and after-task report. R grammar remains reserved until a separate parity and public-contract decision. Protected GLLVM/gllvmTMB lanes and release/submission/GPU work are excluded.

V0 design closure is the present task's only acceptance claim. No V1-V4 implementation or performance evidence is produced here.

    62	hs_fa_decode_vector <- function(value) {
    63	  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0L) return(NULL)
    64	  if (!is.character(value) || is.na(value[[1L]])) return(as.numeric(value))
    65	  encoded <- value[[1L]]
    66	  if (identical(encoded, "__HSQ_NONE__")) return(NULL)
    67	  if (!nzchar(encoded)) return(numeric())
    68	  as.numeric(strsplit(encoded, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]])

    71	hs_fa_decode_matrix <- function(value) {
    72	  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0L) return(NULL)
    73	  if (!is.character(value) || is.na(value[[1L]])) return(value)
    74	  encoded <- value[[1L]]
    75	  if (identical(encoded, "__HSQ_NONE__")) return(NULL)
    76	  dimensions_text <- sub(":.*$", "", encoded)
    77	  dimensions <- as.integer(strsplit(dimensions_text, "x", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]])
    78	  if (length(dimensions) != 2L || anyNA(dimensions)) {
    79	    stop("Internal bridge error: encoded selector matrix has invalid dimensions.", call. = FALSE)
    80	  }
    81	  values_text <- sub("^[^:]*:", "", encoded)
    82	  values <- if (nzchar(values_text)) as.numeric(strsplit(values_text, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]) else numeric()
    83	  if (length(values) != prod(dimensions)) {
    84	    stop("Internal bridge error: encoded selector matrix has invalid value count.", call. = FALSE)
    85	  }
    86	  matrix(values, nrow = dimensions[[1L]], ncol = dimensions[[2L]])
    87	}

   116	hs_fa_rank_rows <- function(rows, schema) {
   117	  fields <- names(schema)
   118	  if (is.null(rows)) rows <- list()
   119	  if (is.data.frame(rows)) rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(rows)), function(i) as.list(rows[i, , drop = FALSE]))
   120	  if (is.list(rows) && length(rows) && !is.null(names(rows)) && all(fields %in% names(rows))) {
   121	    n_rows <- length(rows[[fields[[1L]]]])
   122	    column_cell <- function(column, i, type) {
   123	      if (type == "matrix") {
   124	        if (is.character(column)) return(hs_fa_decode_matrix(column[[i]]))
   125	        dimensions <- dim(column)
   126	        if (length(dimensions) == 3L && dimensions[[3L]] == n_rows) {
   127	          return(column[, , i])
   128	        }
   129	        if (is.list(column) && length(column) == n_rows) return(column[[i]])
   130	        if (n_rows == 1L && length(dimensions) == 2L) return(column)
   131	        if (is.null(column) && n_rows == 1L) return(NULL)
   132	        stop("Internal bridge error: selector covariance column lost row/matrix dimensions.", call. = FALSE)
   133	      }
   134	      if (type == "vector") {
   135	        if (is.character(column)) return(hs_fa_decode_vector(column[[i]]))
   136	        if (is.list(column) && length(column) == n_rows) return(column[[i]])
   137	        if (is.matrix(column) && nrow(column) == n_rows) return(as.numeric(column[i, ]))
   138	        if (is.matrix(column) && ncol(column) == n_rows) return(as.numeric(column[, i]))
   139	        if (is.list(column) && n_rows == 1L) return(column[[1L]])
   140	        if (is.null(column) && n_rows == 1L) return(NULL)
   141	        stop("Internal bridge error: selector vector column lost row dimensions.", call. = FALSE)
   142	      }
   143	      if (is.list(column)) column[[i]] else column[[i]]
   144	    }
   145	    rows <- lapply(seq_len(n_rows), function(i) {
   146	      stats::setNames(lapply(fields, function(field) {
   147	        column_cell(rows[[field]], i, schema[[field]])
   148	      }), fields)
   149	    })
   150	  }
   151	  if (!is.list(rows)) stop("Internal bridge error: selector rows are not a list.", call. = FALSE)
   152	  out <- lapply(fields, function(field) {
   153	    type <- schema[[field]]
   154	    if (type %in% c("matrix", "vector")) {
   155	      I(lapply(rows, function(row) row[[field]]))
   156	    } else {
   157	      vapply(rows, hs_fa_rank_scalar, FUN.VALUE = switch(type,
   158	        numeric = NA_real_, integer = NA_integer_, logical = NA, character = NA_character_
   159	      ), name = field, type = type)
   160	    }
   161	  })
   162	  names(out) <- fields
   163	  as.data.frame(out, optional = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
   164	}

The implementation must write the exact initializer and verify it before fitting. A zero-loading start is excluded because its first-order loading gradient vanishes. No extra retries, changed data, changed floor or hidden warm starts are allowed. Retain the initial attempt even if the retry succeeds.
    61	
    62	Each candidate uses its best eligible converged start within this budget. Eligibility requires finite objective and estimates, positive-definite G and R, the shared floor constraint, convergence, matched inputs/normalization and successful objective reevaluation. A better finite unconverged start exceeding the chosen converged loglik by `tau/2` makes selection unavailable after the one allowed retry. Start covariance disagreement and objective ranges remain visible; they do not certify a global optimum.
    63	
    64	With a matched floor, the FA family contains the diagonal covariance at L=0. If the best eligible FA loglik remains below the diagonal loglik by more than `tau/2`, flag a nesting/optimization failure and refuse selection. The nested witness is an objective evaluation at L=0, not a successful FA optimization claim.

    66	All tau/2 comparisons above use loglik units because tau is defined in criterion units. Both candidate ranks must be eligible to select a rank. If either fails after its budget, return `selection_status=unavailable`, no selected rank/fit, a reason and all attempts. A sole successful candidate does not win by default. The user may request an explicit fixed rank independently; no silent fallback fit is made.

    68	Near-floor candidates can remain eligible under the experimental score, with `boundary_sensitive=true`. The floor flag is defined for both candidates because both now share c. It is not a claim of uniqueness identification. At or numerically below the bound is an admissibility failure. The fixed absolute floor is unit-dependent; no silent standardization, rescaling or new preprocessing is introduced. Unit-change validation must identify where selection changes because constraints change.

    71	
    72	Return `selected_fit` alongside plain selection metadata:
    73	
    74	| Field | Required meaning |
    75	| --- | --- |
    76	| selection_status, reason | selected, unavailable or unsupported_input, with a clear explanation. |
    77	| requested_ranks, selected_rank | Always requested {0,1}; selected integer or missing. |

function _fa_independent_dense_reml(Y, X, A, G, R)
    n, T = size(Y)
    p = size(X, 2)
    order = [i + (j - 1) * n for i in 1:n for j in 1:T]
    y = vec(Y)[order]
    D = zeros(n * T, p * T)
    V = zeros(n * T, n * T)
    for i in 1:n, j in 1:T
        row = (i - 1) * T + j
        for c in 1:p
            D[row, (c - 1) * T + j] = X[i, c]
        end
        for k in 1:n, l in 1:T
            col = (k - 1) * T + l
            V[row, col] = A[i, k] * G[j, l] + (i == k ? R[j, l] : 0.0)
        end
    end

    F = cholesky(Symmetric(V))
    yw = F.L \ y
    Dw = F.L \ D
    C = cholesky(Symmetric(transpose(Dw) * Dw))
    beta = C \ (transpose(Dw) * yw)
    rw = yw - Dw * beta
    logdet_V = 2sum(log, diag(F.L))
    logdet_DtViD = 2sum(log, diag(C.L))
    loglik = -0.5 * ((length(y) - size(D, 2)) * log(2π) +
                     logdet_V + logdet_DtViD + dot(rw, rw))
    return (loglik = loglik, y = y, V = V)
end

function write_validation_status_table!(
    page_path::AbstractString = joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "docs", "src", "validation-status.md");
    status = validation_status(),
)
    page = read(page_path, String)
    occursin(BEGIN_MARK, page) || error("missing begin marker in $page_path")
    occursin(END_MARK, page) || error("missing end marker in $page_path")

    table = validation_status_table_markdown(status)
    block = string(BEGIN_MARK, "\n\n", table, "\n", END_MARK)
    i0 = findfirst(BEGIN_MARK, page)
    i1 = findfirst(END_MARK, page)
    (i0 === nothing || i1 === nothing) && error("markers not found in $page_path")
    i1.start > i0.start || error("end marker precedes begin marker in $page_path")
    updated = string(page[1:(i0.start - 1)], block, page[(i1.stop + 1):end])
    write(page_path, updated)
    return page_path
end

# Bounded automatic genetic FA-rank contract

Status: design frozen for future implementation review, 2026-10-01. No automatic selector is implemented or validated by this document. The current fixed-rank Gaussian FA route remains experimental, and public covered count stays seven. Approved scope and execution record: [design arc](auto-fa-rank-design-plan-20261001.md).

## Model and candidates

The first selector is explicit opt-in and compares only shared genetic factor counts `K={0,1}` for four complete Gaussian traits, pedigree relationships, one record per observed animal, trait intercepts and an unstructured residual covariance. The same records, labels, units, X, Z and Ainv are used for both candidates. Explicit fixed-rank calls keep their current meaning; omission of rank does not invoke selection. Missing responses, other trait counts/ranks, other fixed effects, genomic/custom relationships, repeatability and non-Gaussian models are refused before fitting. K=2 is outside this design.

Write `Y=XB+ZU+E`. For the engine's record-major order, `y=vec(Y')`, `u=vec(U')`, `X_full=X⊗I_4`, `Z_full=Z⊗I_4`,

`Cov(u)=A⊗G_K`, `Cov(vec(E'))=I_n⊗R`,

`V_K=Z_full(A⊗G_K)Z_full'+I_n⊗R`,

`G_K=L_K L_K'+diag(psi)`, `psi_i=c+exp(theta_i)`, `c=1e-4` in squared units of trait i.

| Candidate | Shape and future implementation mapping | Genetic parameters |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| K=0 | Diagonal G with positive trait-specific genetic variances. Selector-internal floor-matched diagonal fit; no loading columns. | 4 |
| K=1 | Existing FA shape with four loadings and four positive uniquenesses; rank-one shared component. | 8 |

K measures shared factors, not the rank of G, which is positive definite when uniquenesses are positive. K=0 still permits genetic variance. Zero genetic signal is a separate boundary case, outside the fitted strictly-positive family.

The existing public diagonal route uses `exp(theta)` without c, while FA uses `c+exp(theta)`. A direct call to the current diagonal fitter is therefore not a floor-matched nested comparator. Future implementation must add the matched internal candidate without changing the public fixed-rank diagonal route, the FA rank guard or the existing floor. It must retain ten identical residual log-Cholesky coordinates in both candidates. Exact source findings: [engine review](../dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/engine-contract.md), `src/multivariate.jl:660-723,844-856,1010-1055` at base `28f90e09`.

Identifiability is a property of the covariance and record design. With one record per animal, Z=I and A=I, only G+R is identifiable. That design is refused for automatic selection; its likelihood is retained as a deterministic negative witness. The identification screen must compare genetic and residual kernels on the REML contrast space: use Q with Q'X_full=0 and inspect Q'V_K Q, not raw A versus I alone. Exact or numerically unresolved proportional kernels on that space must refuse selection with a design-identification reason. For intercept-only one-record data, the informative-looking half-sib matrix A=(1-rho)I+rho*11' becomes (1-rho)I after removing the intercept direction; G and R remain confounded. This is a second deterministic refusal witness. Relatedness alone does not establish good finite-sample information. The future pre-run must freeze a numerical kernel-rank check and its unit convention before real selection fits; no numerical conditioning threshold is claimed validated here.

For general K the nominal genetic dimension is `4K-K(K-1)/2+4`. At K=2 it exceeds the ten-dimensional ambient symmetric G space. This dimension screen does not prove identifiability at K=1. At L=0 the derivative of LL' is zero; diagonal-to-FA nesting is singular, so the score below is not a regular four-df likelihood-ratio test.

## Criterion and numerical comparison

Freeze criterion name `reml_aic_covariance` as an experimental comparison rule on the common fixed-effect contrast space:

`C_K=-2*ell_REML,K+2*q_K`, `q_K=q_G(K)+q_R`, `q_R=10`.

The exact engine REML normalization is

`ell_REML=-0.5*((4n-p_full)*log(2*pi)+logdet(V)+logdet(X_full' V^-1 X_full)+y'P y)`,

`P=V^-1-V^-1 X_full (X_full'V^-1 X_full)^-1 X_full'V^-1`, `p_full=4`.

The four common fixed intercepts are removed by REML and not counted in q. The displayed q values are 14 and 18; penalties are 28 and 36. Counting common intercepts in both penalties would shift scores equally but is not this declared convention. Residual parameters are counted and displayed even though they cancel in the difference.

Define signed difference `D=C_1-C_0=8-2*(ell_1-ell_0)`. Negative D favors K=1. Away from numerical ties, K=1 wins when `2*(ell_1-ell_0)>8`. Report both full C values and D; calculate D directly from the likelihood difference to reduce cancellation. Reevaluate both objectives on the identical input model before ranking.

Freeze numerical tie band `tau=1e-6` criterion units for the initial moderate-scale validation cell. Require each returned loglik to agree with independent same-covariance reevaluation within `1e-8` absolute loglik units before selection. Thus the two objective discrepancies can contribute at most `4e-8` to D under this check, below tau; this discrepancy budget is a check convention, not a proof of all floating-point or optimizer error. If the future pre-run cannot meet it, stop and revise the numerical contract before any campaign. Do not enlarge it after seeing selected ranks.

If `abs(D)<=tau`, choose K=0 and set `near_tie=true`; an exact tie is included. If D is below -tau choose K=1; otherwise choose K=0. Return tau and the objective discrepancies. This band handles numerical ambiguity; it is not an evidence-strength cutoff or a calibrated confidence interval. Weak substantive separation remains visible as the raw D, even when outside tau.

This is a restricted-likelihood covariance comparison with nominal parameter penalties and a singular smaller model. It does not establish consistency, correct biological dimension, marginal predictive optimality or calibrated rank probabilities. Gurka discusses ambiguities in REML model selection; the chosen bounded rule needs its own selection study. [Gurka (2006)](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1198/000313006X90396).

The mixed-model selection review motivates keeping the likelihood target, covariance boundaries and effective sample size explicit. [Müller, Scealy and Welsh (2013)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.2427). BIC is deferred because no pedigree-specific effective sample-size rule has been justified. [Delattre, Lavielle and Poursat (2014)](https://doi.org/10.1214/14-EJS890). The singular boundary also prevents treating D as an ordinary chi-square test. [Self and Liang (1987)](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1987.10478472). These sources motivate limits; none validates this exact selector.

Marginal ML-AIC would require a genuinely fitted ML objective for both candidates. Evaluating ML only at REML estimates is excluded. Conditional AIC, BIC, rank probabilities and automatic criterion switching are outside this first contract.

## Starts, eligibility and failure policy

Fit the floor-matched diagonal candidate from the documented phenotype-based default; fit FA from its existing default and balanced starts. Neither uses generating truth. Permit at most one additional FA retry, only when the initial FA candidate is failed, unconverged or materially non-nested relative to the eligible diagonal candidate, or when a better finite unconverged FA attempt exceeds the best eligible converged FA loglik by more than tau/2. Thus the first budget is one diagonal optimizer start and at most three FA starts, four total. The unequal budget is declared; it does not imply equal optimization robustness.

The additional FA start uses the diagonal covariance as a target with a deterministic, nonzero loading perturbation and corresponding floor-safe uniquenesses, preserving the covariance as closely as feasible. The implementation must write the exact initializer and verify it before fitting. A zero-loading start is excluded because its first-order loading gradient vanishes. No extra retries, changed data, changed floor or hidden warm starts are allowed. Retain the initial attempt even if the retry succeeds.

Each candidate uses its best eligible converged start within this budget. Eligibility requires finite objective and estimates, positive-definite G and R, the shared floor constraint, convergence, matched inputs/normalization and successful objective reevaluation. A better finite unconverged start exceeding the chosen converged loglik by `tau/2` makes selection unavailable after the one allowed retry. Start covariance disagreement and objective ranges remain visible; they do not certify a global optimum.

With a matched floor, the FA family contains the diagonal covariance at L=0. If the best eligible FA loglik remains below the diagonal loglik by more than `tau/2`, flag a nesting/optimization failure and refuse selection. The nested witness is an objective evaluation at L=0, not a successful FA optimization claim.

All tau/2 comparisons above use loglik units because tau is defined in criterion units. Both candidate ranks must be eligible to select a rank. If either fails after its budget, return `selection_status=unavailable`, no selected rank/fit, a reason and all attempts. A sole successful candidate does not win by default. The user may request an explicit fixed rank independently; no silent fallback fit is made.

Near-floor candidates can remain eligible under the experimental score, with `boundary_sensitive=true`. The floor flag is defined for both candidates because both now share c. It is not a claim of uniqueness identification. At or numerically below the bound is an admissibility failure. The fixed absolute floor is unit-dependent; no silent standardization, rescaling or new preprocessing is introduced. Unit-change validation must identify where selection changes because constraints change.

## Returned object and future bridge

Return `selected_fit` alongside plain selection metadata:

| Field | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| selection_status, reason | selected, unavailable or unsupported_input, with a clear explanation. |
| requested_ranks, selected_rank | Always requested {0,1}; selected integer or missing. |
| criterion, criterion_status, q, penalties | reml_aic_covariance, experimental; per-candidate counts and scores. |
| criterion_difference, tie_tolerance, near_tie | D=C1-C0, tau and numerical tie flag. |
| records/design/relationship fingerprint | Demonstrate identical model inputs across candidates. |
| candidate_summary | One row per requested rank, including unattempted/failed ranks and eligibility reason. |
| attempts | One row per start/retry, preserving failures and diagnostic fields. |
| boundary_sensitive, start_sensitive | Visible flags derived from retained fits and attempts. |
| uncertainty_scope | conditional_on_selected_rank; no selection-adjusted uncertainty claim. |

Each attempt row records rank, structure, start ID, retry index, attempted status, failure reason, converged, optimizer status/iterations, finite-value/PD checks, returned and reevaluated loglik, q/criterion when defined, per-trait uniqueness and floor distances, near-floor flags, eligibility and selected marker. Failed values are missing with reasons, never zero. The candidate summary separates the chosen within-rank start from the selected rank.

The candidate_summary is the authoritative retained row for every requested rank, including preflight-unattempted ranks. The attempts table contains actual starts only; no synthetic optimizer-start rows are created for unattempted ranks. Preflight refusals mark both candidate-summary rows unattempted with the reason. Interrupts abort promptly and propagate cancellation; the future wrapper/harness must retain its partial attempt ledger and mark interrupted/unattempted rows without pretending to return a completed selection. The interruption mechanism is an implementation acceptance item, not permission to swallow an interrupt.

Proposed function name `select_fa_rank` is reserved for design discussion. It is not an implemented export or approved R grammar. Any future R expert-control payload must preserve the full table, missing reasons, scores, flags and selected covariance/EBVs in original label order. The existing bounded R fixed-rank transport is verified at immutable R merge `e82f5c95`; automatic-selection fields are new work. [User-contract review](../dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/user-contract.md).

The attempt table shows the comparison and any boundary or start sensitivity. Uncertainty from the fitted model is conditional on this chosen rank.” Avoid describing K as the true number of biological dimensions.

## Freeze and remaining implementation obligations

The candidate set, model shape, experimental score/parameter convention, signed difference, tie rule, strict two-candidate eligibility, retry ceiling and returned semantics are frozen for this bounded implementation proposal. The numerical acceptance tolerances above are predeclared engineering checks, not measured successes.

They are specified acceptance obligations with clear failure outcomes, not current capabilities. Uninformative and weak-information pedigree cases are separate identification/availability cells, not excluded fits that disappear from the denominator.

It never forms/factorizes `C`: each score fixed-point step is a matrix-free PCG solve + a Hutchinson stochastic trace (`mc_reml_block_traces`) for the score-trace `tr(Aᵢ⁻¹C⁻¹[uᵢ,uᵢ])` that the exact `fit_sparse_multi_effect_aireml` reads from a Cholesky selected inverse — so it is not limited by the K≥2 fill-in. Unit-gated (`test/runtests.jl`): the Hutchinson trace is unbiased vs the exact `selinv_block_traces` (within its MC error band); the fit recovers the exact AI-REML optimum to ~0.7% at q=300 nprobe=300; `fit_multi_effect(...; method=:auto)` routes exact-vs-matrix-free by feasibility. PRE-DECLARED recovery+scale gate (DRAC fir job 46725575, `docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-07-02-v08-s2fit-recovery-scale-result.md`): recovery 48 seeds K=3 q=960 PASS (all converged, MC reproduces the covered exact estimator to 2.6% ≤5%, secondary \|bias\|≤2·MCSE max 1.20); scale the FIT converges to q=200,000 (11.5s→586s) — extending the S2 SOLVE feasibility (q=10⁶) to the FIT. EXPERIMENTAL, engine-internal, NOT the public default; APPROXIMATES the exact fit (the stochastic score-trace error is a feasibility trade, with trace-probe standard error reported as `trace_mcse`, ∝1/√nprobe). DELIVERED since: (V8.1) a matrix-free REML `loglik` — `matrix_free_reml_loglik` estimates `log|C|` by stochastic Lanczos quadrature (matrix-free) + remaining determinant terms directly and the quadratic term through PCG, matching the exact `sparse_multi_reml_loglik` within the SLQ MC band (stochastic); (V8.2) trace variance reduction — `shared_probes = true` estimates all K traces from one full-random probe per solve (K× fewer solves, unbiased, tighter at equal budget on the measured fixtures; no general precision guarantee); (V8.3) matrix-free ASYMPTOTIC intervals — `matrix_free_reml_information` (the AI matrix built matrix-free to PCG accuracy, without stochastic traces) + `matrix_free_ratio_intervals` reproduce the exact delta-method ratio/`h²` intervals (asymptotic/uncalibrated); (V8.4) an external SAME-ESTIMAND comparator at VALIDATION SCALE — `comparator/matfree_blupf90_neffect.jl` runs `blupf90+` 2.60 AIREMLF90 live on the shared K=3 fixture (q=860) and the matrix-free across-seed mean reaches blupf90's optimum to ≤0.15% (within MC error; blupf90 within ≤0.5 across-seed SD per component; exact-vs-blupf90 3.8e-5), `docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-07-03-v84-matfree-blupf90-comparator.md`. R CONNECTION (V8.6): the R `target="multi_effect"` `(1|g)` surface can opt into this path via `engine_control scale_method="auto"` (default `"dense"` byte-identical) — validation-scale routes to the sparse-exact (covered) estimator, large-scale to this experimental matrix-free fit; the R covered claim is unchanged. Deferred: COVERAGE-CALIBRATED intervals + the AT-SCALE (large-fixture, exact-infeasible) external comparator leg (`docs/design/25-completion-ultraplan.md`) Fixed probes give seed repeatability. Stopping uses small relative variance-component changes, which do not establish score stationarity, a unique/global optimum, or parameter precision. `trace_mcse` measures trace-probe uncertainty and excludes PCG error; it is not variance-component uncertainty. Multi-effect `loglik` is NaN when disabled; when requested it is a stochastic full-REML SLQ estimate. Its Monte-Carlo standard error excludes finite-Lanczos bias and PCG error. Historical q=4060 BLUPF90 agreement (exact fit 4.7e-6; matrix-free across-seed differences 0.95% at nprobe=128 and 0.71% at nprobe=256) is recorded in `docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-07-03-v84-atscale-comparator.md`; it does not discharge the large-fixture, exact-infeasible external comparator debt. New source/scale/design recovery claims require fresh evidence. |
docs/design/capability-status.md:88:| Matrix-free Monte-Carlo single-effect REML (`V1-MATFREE-REML`, `fit_matrix_free_reml`) | experimental | `fit_matrix_free_reml(spec)` estimates the two variance components of the univariate Gaussian animal model by matrix-free stochastic REML score fixed-point iteration: matrix-free PCG solves plus the Hutchinson stochastic score trace (`mc_reml_block_traces`), so the MME coefficient matrix `C` is NEVER assembled or factorized during the fit. It targets the ONE regime the Wave-F F0 measurement found infeasible for the exact path — HIGH fill-in AND `n` past the dense eigen cap — where the per-iteration Takahashi selected inverse, not the Cholesky, is the wall (q=20,000 / fill 471: 381s of a 1529s fit against a 0.35s factorization). It is the `K=1` case of the already-committed v0.8-S2 matrix-free multi-effect machinery — an `AnimalModelFit`-returning adapter, NOT new numerics — and returns the standard fit object (`target = :matrix_free_reml`), whose `loglik` is the EXACT `sparse_reml_loglik` evaluated once at the returned estimate when enabled, even if the iteration did not report convergence; `compute_loglik = false` returns NaN. **The estimator is STOCHASTIC:** it uses Monte-Carlo score traces (trace error proportional to `1/sqrt(nprobe)`); fixed probes give repeatability for a supplied `seed`. **PROVENANCE — this is a PORT.** The fitter body is byte-identical to the v0.7 lineage (`33ab68f6`) and was ported by `f261165e` so the frozen S5 gate could run on a `main`-based campaign branch. **The v0.7 in-CI deterministic NUMERIC gates are PINNED as of 2026-09-02** (`test/test_matfree_reml_inci_pins.jl`: exact-loglik identity to 1e-12, seed determinism / sensitivity, extractors, `compute_loglik = false` NaN skip) — a path / identity pin, NOT a recovery or covered flip. **The opt-in fence is PINNED IN CI as of 2026-09-01** (testset `V1-MATFREE-REML opt-in fence`): `fit_animal_model` is asserted to refuse `:matrix_free`, `:matrix_free_reml`, `:matrix_free_mc_em_reml`, and `:auto`; the accepted target surface is pinned closed at four canonical targets; `_auto_reml_route` is asserted absent; and no `src/` module beyond the definition, the export list, and the ledger names the fitter. So it is reachable ONLY by direct call, and re-wiring a route now fails loudly. That fence is scoped to the ANIMAL-MODEL target router: `fit_multi_effect(method = :auto)` is a different estimator (`V3-NEFFECT-MATFREE-FIT`) and does route to a matrix-free engine, so `:auto` is not matrix-free-free package-wide. **S5 TAIL-SCALE RECOVERY GATE — PASS (2026-09-01):** pre-declared before running, q=25,000, 48 seeds, Julia 1.10.10 on Totoro; CONVERGED 48/48, mean rel.err vs generating TRUTH 0.0016/0.0007 (bound 0.05), NON_GRACEFUL 0/48, CAP_EXHAUSTED 0/48, Leg X vs exact `fit_ai_reml` 0.0090/0.0052; byte-identical on independent re-invocation. A non-pre-declared Julia 1.12.6 arm also passes but gives A1 `sigma_a2` 0.0142, so the honest margin across the two realizations measured is **~3.5x, not ~30x**. **NO capability flip from this row; live R-public `public_covered_count` is **7**.** Still owed before any promotion: the AT-SCALE external comparator (S6 — the ASReml-R 4.2.0.482 leg agrees to 1.31e-7 but ran at q=2000 / fill 75.2, BELOW the ~150 crossover, i.e. where the exact path still wins), a fresh promote-specific Rose audit (S4), the R bridge (S7), and maintainer G10 sign-off (S3, UNSIGNED). Fixed probes give seed repeatability. Stopping uses small relative variance-component changes, which do not establish score stationarity, a unique/global optimum, or parameter precision. `trace_mcse` measures trace-probe uncertainty and excludes PCG error; it is not variance-component uncertainty. Historical lineage identity and S5 results above retain their original pins; they are not new recovery evidence for the current source. |

docs/design/capability-status.md:107:| K-effect variance-component standard errors and summed-ratio interval | experimental | `multi_effect_variance_component_covariance` builds the asymptotic covariance of `[σ₁²,…,σ_K², σ_e²]` as the inverse of a central finite-difference Hessian of the SPARSE `sparse_multi_reml_loglik`, so it applies at the scale `fit_multi_effect(:auto)` fits and never densifies `Aᵢ⁻¹`; `multi_effect_variance_component_standard_errors`, `multi_effect_ratio_standard_errors` (delta method on `σᵢ²/Σσ²`) and `multi_effect_sum_ratio_interval` (logit-scale delta CI for a SUMMED ratio, e.g. repeatability `(σ²a+σ²pe)/Σ`) derive from it, and `multi_effect_uncertainty` returns all three from ONE information matrix. Correctness is agreement with an INDEPENDENT dense computation — the covariance from `_multi_effect_dense`, which densifies `Ainv` (`test/test_352_multi_effect_se.jl`); the K=1 ratio reduces to `h²`; level nesting, rail/boundary behaviour and the argument guards are pinned. It REFUSES rather than returning `NaN` when the information is not finite positive-definite, or when a component sits too close to zero for the finite-difference step (boundary optimum). Consumed by the R twin's `target = "repeatability"`, `scale_method = "auto"` route. PERFORMANCE (2026-09-21, measured on one machine, bitwise-identical output): the three derived quantities each rebuilt the same Hessian, and every Hessian evaluation rebuilt the σ-independent conversions, cross-products, `log|Aᵢ⁻¹|` and the CHOLMOD symbolic analysis. A shared workspace (`_MultiREMLWorkspace`: hoisted σ-invariant terms, in-place `nzval` assembly, symbolic reuse through `cholesky!`) and an upper-triangle-only finite-difference loop (36 → 24 evaluations; `Symmetric` discarded the other 12) take one evaluation 43.2 ms → 9.08 ms and the three calls 4.37 s → 0.60 s on an 11,856-record / 10,937-animal animal + permanent-environment fit, 0.17 s through `multi_effect_uncertainty`. Verified BITWISE against the pre-change code (loglik, BLUPs, the full covariance, every SE, the interval endpoints); `test/test_post_fit_uncertainty_reuse.jl`. docs/design/capability-status.md:108:| Direct–maternal genetic model (2×2 G, first correlated random effect) (Phase 4) | covered | `fit_direct_maternal_reml(y, X, Zd, Zm, Ainv)` estimates the 2×2 direct–maternal genetic covariance `G_dm` over `[a_d; a_m]` (one trait, one relationship `A`, DIRECT incidence `Zd`=record→animal, MATERNAL incidence `Zm`=record→dam; `Var = kron(G_dm, A)`, marginal `V = W·kron(G_dm,A)·Wᵀ + σ²e I`) + `σ²e` by dense REML (log-Cholesky, reusing the multivariate `_chol_params_to_cov`). FIRST correlated structure (`σ_dm ≠ 0`), distinct from independent multi-effect and multivariate-G0. Correctness (`test/runtests.jl:7366`): a diagonal `G_dm` (`σ_dm=0`) is byte-identical to the two-independent-effect model (~1e-9); a full 2×2 `G_dm` (incl. negative off-diagonal) matches a marginal-GLS oracle (~1e-9, observed ~1e-15); the fit returns a PD `G_dm` + `r_am ∈ [-1,1]`, and honestly reports `converged=false` on tiny/non-identified data. **Covered** (experimental, validation-scale, OPT-IN; NOT the public default fit path) via the doc-16 substitutable gate: a PRE-DECLARED 48-seed bias/MCSE gate (`sim/phase4_direct_maternal_recovery_gate.jl`, predeclared `76f6c67e` BEFORE the run — harness byte-identical; n=960, 90 identifying dams, confound-broken DGP) PASSED — 48/48 converged, all four `|bias|≤2·MCSE` (σ²_ad 0.13, σ²_am 1.65, σ_dm 0.72, σ²e 0.24; max cond 157, max |r_am| 0.80, no boundary rides) — plus a `sommer` 4.4.5 `covm()` same-estimand REML comparator AGREE (ABSOLUTE-variance + column-identified: σ_dm 1.1e-2, other entries ≤4.2e-3 rel.diff). Evidence: `docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-07-01-direct-maternal-covered-evidence.md`. "Covered" = the engine correctly implements direct–maternal 2×2-`G` REML on the tested confound-broken design, NOT small-sample accuracy of any single component. INTERPRETATION FENCE (Willham): a negative `r_am` is real and expected; direct h² (`σ²_ad/σ_P`) is NOT "the heritability" — the selection-relevant total additive variance involves `σ_dm` (`σ_P = σ²_ad + σ²_am + σ_dm + σ²e`); the R surface returns the labelled triple (direct h², m², Willham total h²_T), never a bare scalar. SCOPE: SINGLE relationship `A` (NOT the maternal-A2 generalization); dense/validation-scale n≤~1000; `|r_am|→1` rides on `converged`. Owed (covered does NOT retire): broader-DGP / larger-scale recovery, the production sparse AI-REML path, a Mrode Ch.7 fitted anchor, CALIBRATED (coverage-validated) intervals. A 2nd INDEPENDENT same-estimand comparator on a different lineage is now DISCHARGED — `blupf90+` 2.60 AIREMLF90 2×2-G via `OPTIONAL mat` (2026-07-02) converged from a neutral start to the engine optimum ~3e-5 on all four entries (dam-identification verified, ABSOLUTE-variance + column-identified; `docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-07-02-direct-maternal-blupf90-comparator.md`; WOMBAT/ASReml optional further legs); asymptotic delta-method SEs/CIs are now provided by `direct_maternal_interval` (VCs + r_am Fisher-z + Willham triple, observed-information FD-Hessian, uncalibrated — corroborated by BLUPF90's AI-based SEs to ~4–12% (max 11.5%)). An R `maternal_genetic()` / `target="direct_maternal"` surface exists and is opt-in covered; engine-covered ≠ R-public-covered (the 5th `public_covered_count` is the R-public surface). docs/design/capability-status.md:154:| Non-Gaussian latent/observation-scale heritability (Phase 6, H7) | experimental | `nongaussian_heritability(fit; mu, n_trials, predictor_variance)` + `nongaussian_heritability(sigma_a2, mu, family::ResponseFamily; predictor_variance)` (EXPORTED) — the Nakagawa–Schielzeth (2017) / de Villemereuil (QGglmm) latent- and observation-scale h² transform. Latent h² = V_A/(V_A + V_link + V_fixed), V_link = π²/3 (logit) / σ²e (Gaussian) / 0 (Poisson log → latent h² NaN, degenerate) / **ψ₁(shape) = trigamma (Gamma log → NON-degenerate latent h², EXACT = Var[log Y], doc-19 §3.1; `method = :gamma_trigamma_latent`)**. Observation/data scale: V_A,obs = Ψ²·V_A (Ψ = average inverse-link derivative; Stein → 0<h²_obs<1), integrated over the LINEAR-PREDICTOR distribution N(μ, V_A+V_fixed) by the module's existing 20-node Gauss–Hermite (logit, proportion estimand) or the log-normal closed form (Poisson, count estimand) — the π²/3 logit residual is NOT added to the integration variance (matching QGglmm `binom1.logit`). Validated (`test/runtests.jl`): Gaussian reduction (machine precision), logit latent closed form (1e-12), logit observation vs an INDEPENDENT 64-node quadrature (rtol 1e-3, 0<h²<1), Poisson degeneracy + closed form vs integration (rtol 1e-6), the n_trials information gradient (h²_obs rises 1→5→20), and guards (non-converged refused, per-record n_trials → NaN+caveat, ambiguous μ throws, Bernoulli information_limited). THRESHOLD families (`:bernoulli_probit`, `:ordered_probit`) report the LIABILITY scale (= latent, V_link = 1; Dempster–Lerner 1950) `V_A/(V_A+1+V_fixed)` in `h2_latent` (μ- and cutpoint-independent, `method = :probit_liability`; validated closed-form incl. the exact K=2 ordinal→bernoulli-probit reduction + the V_fixed denominator). The BINARY (`:bernoulli_probit`) observed-0/1 scale is computed via the QGglmm probit integration over `η~N(μ,V_A+V_fixed)` (`Ψ²V_A/[p̄(1−p̄)]`, `p̄=E[Φ(η)]`, `Ψ=E[φ(η)]`) — verified EQUAL to the Dempster–Lerner transform `z²/[p(1−p)]` (`test/runtests.jl`, ≈1e-6) and `< h²_liab`; the ORDINAL (K>2) per-category observed scale is now computed as the VECTOR `h2_observation_by_category` (`h²_k = Ψ_k²V_A/[p_k(1−p_k)]` per category indicator, `p_k=E[Φ(θ_k−η)−Φ(θ_{k-1}−η)]`, `Ψ_k=E[φ(θ_{k-1}−η)−φ(θ_k−η)]`, over `η~N(μ,V_A+V_fixed)`; the scalar `h2_observation` stays NaN — no single ordinal observed h²), VALIDATED to ≤3e-8 vs QGglmm `model=ordinal` (`comparator/qgglmm_ordinal_observed/`; incl. the K=2 reduction to the binary observed h²). GAMMA DATA/observation scale now computed too: `h²_obs = V_A/[e^{V_pred}(1+1/ν)−1]` (the NS-2017 multiplicative form; μ-independent lognormal closed form), VALIDATED against QGglmm's custom Gamma-log model (var.func μ²/ν) to ~5e-11 (`comparator/qgglmm_gamma_observed/`; `test/runtests.jl`). Dependency-free; NOT added to the family-uniform `nongaussian_result_payload`. EXPORTED but experimental. The QGglmm EXTERNAL comparator is RUN + AGREES (≤4.5e-6, 25 comparisons) for the logit + binary-probit + Poisson(count) + Binomial(n>1) observation scales (all four QGglmm builtins; `comparator/qgglmm_probit_observed/`, `QGparams(model=binom1.{logit,probit}/Poisson.log/binomN.logit)`; doc-19 §5), the ordinal K>2 observed scale (≤3e-8 via `model=ordinal`; `comparator/qgglmm_ordinal_observed/`), and the Gamma-data observation scale (~5e-11 via QGglmm's custom Gamma model; `comparator/qgglmm_gamma_observed/`); still owed: an MCMCglmm comparator and a Fisher/Falconer sign-off; plus beta-binomial/negative-binomial families, intervals, and R activation pending; not the public default, not covered. `V6-NS-H2` |
docs/design/capability-status.md:157:| Genetic-GLLVM integrated-Laplace fitting (estimate latent G_lat) (Phase 6, #50) | experimental | `fit_gllvm_laplace_reml(Y, Ainv, family; rank, X)` (internal) ESTIMATES the rank-`K` latent loadings `Λ` (`G_lat = ΛΛ'`) by maximizing the K-factor fixed-and-genetic-effect integrated Laplace objective (`gllvm_laplace_marginal_loglik`) over `vec(Λ)` (NelderMead). The marginal depends on `Λ` only through `G_lat = ΛΛ'`, so it is rotation-invariant — the result reports the rotation-INVARIANT `genetic_covariance` / `latent_structure`, never the raw `Λ̂`. Validated (`test/runtests.jl`): the `K=1, T=1` Poisson case reduces to the single-factor `fit_laplace_reml` (`σ²a = λ̂²`, rtol 2e-3); a multi-trait Poisson rank-1 fit converges with the optimum improving over the start; and the Gaussian optimum's marginal equals `_multivariate_reml_loglik` at the estimated `Λ̂Λ̂'` (`R0 = σ²e·I`, rtol 1e-7). A `structure = :factor_analytic` option additionally estimates a per-trait specific genetic variance `Ψ > 0` (`G_lat = ΛΛ' + diag(Ψ)`, fitted on the `log` scale by augmenting the loadings to `[Λ | diag(√Ψ)]` and reusing the marginal unchanged); validated by Gaussian self-consistency at `Ĝ = Λ̂Λ̂'+Ψ̂`, `communality < 1` (since `Ψ̂ > 0`), `FA loglik ≥ low-rank loglik` on the checked fixture (pure low-rank lies in the closure of the positive-Ψ FA model), a converging Poisson FA fit, and length/structure guards. A correctness-validated ESTIMATOR (reductions + optimum-improvement + Gaussian self-consistency). An opt-in known-truth recovery harness (`sim/phase6_gllvm_recovery.jl`, outside CI; `docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-06-20-genetic-gllvm-reml-recovery.md`) now records FOUR scenarios across THREE response families: **(A) Poisson rank-1** (`q=240`): **5/5, mean rel `0.091`**; **(B) Poisson rank-2 NON-degenerate-ρ** (`q=120`): **5/5, mean rel `0.205`, genetic correlations `mean|Δρ| = 0.089`** (loose gate `rel ≤ 0.45`); **(C) Bernoulli rank-1 logit** (`Λ=[0.9,0.6,0.4]`, `μ=0`, `q=240`): **REPORTED-NOT-GATED — mean rel `0.540`, 3/5 below threshold, one seed rel `1.15`** — the observed unsigned relative error on the latent `G_lat` scale; five seeds do not establish bias direction or cause; **(D) Binomial(20) rank-1 logit** (same DGP, `m=20` trials): **5/5, mean rel `0.104`** — a descriptive five-seed contrast that does not establish a trial-count cause. All 20 fits converged. **Consumability additions (2026-06-20):** `family` now accepts a length-`T` `Vector{ResponseFamily}` (per-trait families) as well as a scalar `ResponseFamily` — a uniform vector gives numerically identical objective values to the scalar path; validated by exact `genetic_covariance` equality and convergence of a mixed `[PoissonResponse(), GaussianResponse(1.0)]` fit on the 8-animal fixture. `fit_gllvm_laplace_reml` returns a typed **`GeneticGLLVMFit`** struct (internal) instead of a bare `NamedTuple`, exposing typed extractor methods `genetic_covariance(fit)` (rotation-invariant `G_lat`), `breeding_values(fit)` (`q×T` trait genetic conditional modes on the link scale, including factor-analytic specific modes), `latent_structure(fit)` (the `genetic_gllvm_descriptors` NamedTuple including `communality`), and `loglik(fit)` — all dispatching on the concrete struct type, not on `NamedTuple`, so they do NOT collide with the multivariate extractors; field access `fit.fieldname` is unchanged. All 19 new assertions in `test/runtests.jl` (testset "Genetic-GLLVM consumability") pass; all 21 prior REML testset assertions pass with the new return type. For `GaussianResponse(σ²e)` the scalar residual `σ²e` is FIXED (not estimated); balanced/fully-observed `Y`, INTERNAL (not exported); a bounded R Poisson-log, T=3, rank-2 expert-control bridge calls this fitter. A separate frozen 50-seed ordinary-start Poisson `T=3, K=2` replay was rerun against the pinned current fitter source and passed 50/50; it reuses the 50 seeds from the September ordinary-start primary run and is one-cell reproducibility/usability evidence, not an independent 100-fit study, calibration, broad recovery, or EBV accuracy. The older four-scenario June harness used true-loading starts and is separate evidence (`docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-09-29-gllvm-current-source-replay.md`). Broader R formula/model grammar, FA(+Ψ) and mixed-family recovery, and external same-objective comparator parity remain open; this row is not covered. `V6-GGLLVM-LAPLACE` |
