docs/design/validation-debt-register.md:67:| V1-SELINV-PEV | Sparse selected-inversion PEV/reliability | partial | `prediction_error_variance`/`reliability` accept `method = :selinv` (Takahashi selected inverse of the sparse MME coefficient matrix, kernel adapted from DRM.jl MIT); the selected-inverse PEV diagonal matches the dense MME inverse diagonal to machine precision (well-conditioned validation-scale fits) on a tiny 3-animal pedigree (supplied-variance MME + `AnimalModelFit` paths) and on an 8-animal Mrode9-shaped pedigree with `nfixed = 2` (`AnimalModelFit` path, PEV-diagonal + reliability parity), and on a larger 110-animal 4-generation pedigree (`nfixed = 2`, off-diagonal `Ainv` nnz = 550; PEV-diagonal + reliability parity to rtol 1e-8), `test/runtests.jl`; the fused `selinv_trace_against` (used by `fit_ai_reml` for the `tr(A⁻¹C^uu)` REML score) equals the prior `sum(Ainv .* takahashi_selinv(...)[uu])` to rtol 1e-10 on tiny + 8-animal fixtures and leaves `fit_ai_reml`'s optimum unchanged (`test/runtests.jl`); the `:selinv` PEV/reliability is now the path used to populate the standard `result_payload(::AnimalModelFit)` bridge fields (`V1-RESULT`); **boundary hardening (#6)**: `prediction_error_variance(:selinv) ≈ :dense` (atol 1e-8) and `reliability(:selinv) ≈ :dense` (atol 1e-8) confirmed on a highly-inbred pedigree (selfing chain, F up to 0.875, 8 animals) — selinv stays numerically exact under high inbreeding; correctness-at-boundary only, NO performance claim. **Memory/perf fix (Szymek, `6bb10c97`, landed on `main` ahead of #350 and carried through the #355 rebase):** `reliability`'s `A_ii = diag(inv(Ainv))` denominator previously formed the DENSE `n×n` `A = inv(Ainv)` UNCONDITIONALLY, regardless of the requested `method`. A user report (ASReml-R comparison, ~100,000-animal pedigree, ~35 GB observed) prompted this fix; a local, non-committed, synthetic 100,000-animal pedigree (window-mated for realistic sparse fill, not the user's own data) confirms the mechanism: the old dense path would need >= 80 GB for one `n×n` matrix, the sparse path (a Takahashi selected inverse of `Ainv`'s own sparse Cholesky factor) completes using ~1.15 GB (~70x less), though it is still slow in absolute terms (~142 s single-threaded at that size — a separate, still-open performance debt distinct from the memory fix); an adversarial fully-random-mating synthetic pedigree measured far worse at smaller n (485s at only n=20,000) — the cost tracks pedigree fill-in (mating locality), not just animal count. `accuracy()` now forwards `method` (previously it silently dropped to `:dense` regardless of the fit's own scale); `:selinv` also throws `ArgumentError` (wrapping the underlying `PosDefException`) on a non-positive-definite `Ainv` where `:dense` returns a finite-but-meaningless value — a genuine, documented behavior difference, not just a performance one. A genomic `Ginv` is fully dense, so it is routed to the same dense computation `:dense` uses regardless of requested `method` — sparse-factorizing a dense `Ginv` measured 68-189x SLOWER at n=400-1200 (Gauss review), a real regression this closes. A direct selected-inverse-diagonal vs. the exact analytic `diag(inv(Ainv)) = 1 + F` identity at n=3000, and a bitwise pin of the `fit_ai_reml` cross-product-caching perf fix against its prior per-iteration rebuild, are committed regression tests. **#350 (this branch, rebased onto the above):** `:selinv` (resolved via `:auto`) is now the DEFAULT of both extractors (`:dense` stays the explicit oracle) and the `reliability` denominator `diag(inv(Ainv))` is read through the selected inverse of `Ainv` by default for a sparse (pedigree) `Ainv` — equals `1 + F_i` for a pedigree `Ainv`, `diag(G) + ridge` for a genomic `Ginv`, which stays on the dense path under `:auto`; pinned in `test/test_selinv_defaults_350.jl` — parity to the dense oracle (every entry, atol 1e-8) on a q = 1,000 half-sib `fit_ai_reml` fit and a `result_payload` + `breeding_values_plot_data` budget (< 100 MB, < 1 s at q = 3,000; measured 31.6 MB / 0.007 s vs 962.5 MB / 3.74 s before). `fitted_values(fit)` no longer densifies `Z` (`Matrix{Float64}(spec.Z)`, an `O(n_obs × n_animals)` blow-up; filed as #356, closed as a duplicate of #355, which fixes it); `henderson_mme` solves the SPD MME via generic sparse LU (`lhs \ rhs`) rather than `cholesky(Symmetric(lhs))`, measured 60x slower with more factor fill at n=4000, and pays this twice per `result_payload` (once via `breeding_values`, once via `fitted_values`); neither `prediction_error_variance` nor `reliability` has a `max_dense_cells`-style guard on their `:dense` path, so a direct large-`n` call with `method = :dense` still silently attempts the `O(n³)` inversion with no early, named error. Open debt tracked elsewhere: `henderson_mme` UMFPACK LU paid twice per payload (**#357**), the unreconciled DRAC figure (**#358**), and the missing real-pedigree / external-comparator measurement (**#359**); still needs production-scale/large-pedigree (10⁴–10⁵ animal) validation ON A REAL PEDIGREE and external comparator checks |

docs/design/validation-debt-register.md:106:| V6-BETABINOMIAL | Non-Gaussian beta-binomial / overdispersed-logit family (Phase 6, H2) | partial | `BetaBinomialResponse(n_trials, rho)` (internal) adds an OVERdispersed binomial family (logit link): the success probability is Beta-distributed across records with intra-class correlation `ρ ∈ (0,1)` (`ρ → 0` is the Binomial limit), marginalised in closed form to `ℓ(y\|η,ρ) = lbeta(α+y, β+n−y) − lbeta(α,β) + log C(n,y)` with `α = p(1−ρ)/ρ`, `β = (1−p)(1−ρ)/ρ`, `p = logistic(η)`. Laplace marginal path ONLY; the conditional kernel reuses the module's existing `_loggamma` (Lanczos, `multivariate.jl`) via a new `_lbeta` and a series `_digamma` — no `SpecialFunctions`. The IRLS working weight is the FISHER (expected) information `E[(dℓ/dη)²] = Σ_k score(k,η)²·P(k\|η,ρ)`, NOT the observed `−d²ℓ/dη²`: the logit beta-binomial is concave in `p` but NOT log-concave in `η`, and the observed information DOES go negative at larger `n` in the surprising tail (confirmed at `m=20, ρ=0.5, y=0, η=3` → `−d²ℓ/dη² ≈ −0.099`), which would break `cholesky(Symmetric(H))`; the Fisher information is `≥ 0` by construction so the working system stays PD. The final Laplace determinant uses observed joint curvature at the mode and rejects a non-positive-definite Hessian; independent finite-difference checks cover the beta-binomial and GLLVM paths (`test/wave2_nongaussian_contracts.jl`). Validated (`test/runtests.jl`): the `ρ→0` reduction of both `_fam_loglik` and the Fisher weight to `BinomialResponse(m)` (the binding trusted-path anchor), conditional score == central finite differences (rtol 1e-5), the pmf integrating to 1 with mean `n·p` and the closed-form overdispersed variance `n·p(1−p)(1+(n−1)ρ)`, a zero-mean score with `Fisher weight == E[score²]`, a strictly positive Fisher weight across a wide `(ρ,y,η)` grid including the negative-observed regime, guards (`n_trials<1` / `ρ∉(0,1)` / `y∉0:n_trials`), and a β-fixed INDEPENDENT tensor Gauss–Hermite quadrature of the TRUE beta-binomial marginal close to the Laplace value on the 3-animal fixture; `fit_laplace_reml(...; family = :beta_binomial, n_trials, rho)` estimates `sigma_a2` (Brent) at a SUPPLIED FIXED ρ (both keywords required; `marginal = :variational` rejected), and `nongaussian_result_payload` self-describes the fit with `family = "beta_binomial"` and the fixed ρ in a new `dispersion` field. An opt-in seeded recovery harness (`sim/phase6_betabinomial_recovery.jl`, outside CI; checkpoint `docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-06-22-h2-betabinomial-recovery.md`) on 5 pre-declared seeds (q = 345, m = 20, ρ = 0.2 supplied at truth) passes the hard gate 5/5 (converged ∧ interior σ̂²a ∧ EBV cor 0.74–0.82) and the σ̂²a magnitude recovered well (mean 0.949 vs 1.0, mean rel 0.153, 5/5 within rel ≤ 0.45 reported-not-gated) — m = 20 makes the overdispersed fit informative, conditional on a correctly supplied ρ. Still needs joint `(sigma_a2, ρ)` estimation, a VA/ELBO kernel, a per-record `BetaBinomialVectorResponse`, a `sigma_a2` profile interval (H6), an external comparator (MCMCglmm/aods3/glmmTMB), latent-scale h², and an R `beta_binomial()` formula/bridge activation; INTERNAL (not exported), not the public default, not covered |
docs/design/validation-debt-register.md:107:| V6-PROBIT | Non-Gaussian probit / threshold (liability-scale) family (Phase 6, H3) | partial | `BernoulliProbitResponse` (internal) extends the non-Gaussian engine to a BINARY threshold (liability-scale) animal model with the probit link `P(y=1) = Φ(η)` (liability `η + e`, `e ~ N(0,1)`, observed `y = 1[liability > 0]`). With `s = 2y−1`: conditional `ℓ = log Φ(sη)`, score `s·φ(sη)/Φ(sη)` (signed inverse-Mills), IRLS weight `M(sη)·(M(sη)+sη) ∈ (0,1)`. The probit conditional is LOG-CONCAVE, so its observed information is strictly positive and equals the expected information — no Fisher-scoring substitution (contrast beta-binomial). Dependency-free standard-normal primitives added (`_norm_pdf`/`_norm_logpdf`/`_norm_logcdf`/`_norm_mills`): `Φ`/`erfc` reuse the module's validated incomplete-gamma (`erfc(z)=Q(½,z²)`) and a LOG-form continued fraction keeps `_norm_logcdf` FINITE into the deep tail (`x=−40`); the coarse genomic `_standard_normal_cdf_approx` (7.5e-8) is NOT reused for derivatives. Validated (`test/runtests.jl`): `Φ` matches standard values to 1e-12; `_norm_logcdf` finite at `x=−10/−20/−40` with `Φ(x)+Φ(−x)=1`; the log-form tail cf agrees with the package `Q`; conditional score AND weight match central finite differences (rtol 1e-5); the weight is strictly positive across a `(y,η)` grid incl. `η=−6`; the Laplace mode is stationary; a β-fixed INDEPENDENT Gauss–Hermite quadrature of the TRUE probit marginal is close to the Laplace value on the 3-animal fixture (binary gap documented); `fit_laplace_reml(...; family = :bernoulli_probit)` estimates `sigma_a2` (Brent) and converges; `laplace_reml_interval(...; family = :bernoulli_probit)` returns the clamp-flagged interval; `nongaussian_result_payload` carries `family = "bernoulli_probit"` with NO heritability (liability scale); a non-{0,1} guard throws. LAPLACE ONLY — the probit variational expected information is response-dependent (`−E[ℓ″]` varies with `s`), which the response-free `_fam_expected_weight` signature cannot carry; `marginal = :variational` is rejected (VA is follow-up). Opt-in recovery `sim/phase6_threshold_recovery.jl` (liability DGP, outside CI; checkpoint `docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-06-22-threshold-recovery.md`): 5 pre-declared seeds (q = 345) pass the hard gate 5/5 (EBV cor 0.61–0.76), σ̂²a magnitude reported-not-gated and below truth in this five-seed run (mean 0.633 vs 1.0, ~37% low, 3/5 within rel ≤ 0.45); this does not establish bias direction or cause. Still needs ORDINAL (≥3 categories, estimated cutpoints), a VA kernel, the observation-scale h² transform (H7), a same-estimand external comparator (MCMCglmm `threshold`/ASReml-R/Mrode Ch.10 anchor), and an R `probit` activation. INTERNAL (not exported), binary single-threshold, not the public default, not covered |
docs/design/validation-debt-register.md:108:| V6-ORDINAL | Non-Gaussian ordered-categorical probit (ordinal threshold) family (Phase 6, T1) | covered (scoped) | `OrderedProbitResponse(thresholds)` (internal) generalizes `BernoulliProbitResponse` to K ORDERED categories `1..K` on a standard-normal latent scale with `K-1` SUPPLIED, strictly-increasing cutpoints `θ`: liability `l = η + e`, `e ~ N(0,1)`, `P(y=k|η) = Φ(θ_k−η) − Φ(θ_{k-1}−η)` (`θ_0=−∞`, `θ_K=+∞`). The conditional `ℓ = log P(y|η)` is LOG-CONCAVE in η (log of a Gaussian interval probability), so the score `(φ(θ_{k-1}−η) − φ(θ_k−η))/P` and the OBSERVED-information IRLS weight `score² − (a·φ(a) − b·φ(b))/P` are exact and the weight is `> 0` — same convention as the binary probit (no Fisher-scoring substitution). The interval probability `Φ(b)−Φ(a)` is evaluated in whichever tail avoids 1−1 cancellation, reusing the validated tail-stable `_norm_logcdf`/`_norm_pdf` (with an explicit `_norm_cdf(±∞)` short-circuit). Validated (`test/runtests.jl`, T1): the `K=2, θ=[0]` REDUCTION to `BernoulliProbitResponse` is EXACT for loglik, score, AND observed weight (category 2 ↔ `y=1`); on a 3-category family the probabilities sum to 1, the score is zero-mean (`Σ_k P(k)·score(k)=0`), the score matches a central finite difference of the loglik (rtol 1e-5), the observed weight matches `−(second finite difference)` and is `> 0` (rtol 1e-3); an END-TO-END gate confirms the ordinal Laplace marginal at `θ=[0]` equals the Bernoulli-probit marginal on the same binary data recoded `1/2` (`laplace_marginal_loglik`, Δ ~1e-16); strictly-increasing / non-empty threshold and `1:K` category-range guards throw. A ≥3-category ordinal design is MORE informative than binary (the calving-ease trait, T1). JOINT ESTIMATION (doc-20 Step 1) now landed: `fit_laplace_reml(...; family = :ordered_probit)` optimizes σ²a and K−2 free cutpoint spacings, returns K−1 cutpoints, and obtains β from the joint mode via the IDENTIFIED reparam (fix `θ_1=0`, estimate `θ_2..θ_{K-1}` through positive increments `exp(δ)` → strict ordering automatic; K read from the data), with a guarded outer NelderMead (σ²a safety-rail `|log σ²a − log σ²a₀| ≤ 8` + a singular/non-finite penalty so the weakly-identified small-data MLE cannot run to the boundary). Validated (`test/runtests.jl`, T1 fit): the K=2 fit reduces EXACTLY to `family=:bernoulli_probit` (σ²a rtol 1e-3, marginal loglik atol 1e-5, `cutpoints==[0]`); the K=3 fit on a structured pedigree gives strictly-ordered cutpoints, a rail-bounded σ²a, a self-consistent marginal loglik, and `converged`; `<1`/non-integer-code + `:variational` guards throw. STILL OWED: the `:symbol` payload (`nongaussian_result_payload` cutpoints + scale-labelled h²); a VA kernel; a deep-latent-tail log-space `logsubexp` loglik; the observation-/liability-scale h² transform. The pre-declared recovery gate is now **PASSED (2026-07-01, 48 seeds)**: known-truth A=I/repeated-records K=3 recovery on an INFORMATIVE design (`sim/phase6_ordinal_recovery.jl`, q=120×4=480 obs, predeclared `3bef5b03` before the run) — 48/48 converged, `|bias| ≤ 2·MCSE` for σ²a (bias +0.027, **1.44·MCSE** — the weak axis, small-sample threshold pull), the cutpoint θ_2 (essentially exact, 0.58·MCSE), AND β; no detectable bias (`docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-07-01-ordinal-recovery-48seed.md`); the informative design resolves the Phase-1 small-data weak-identification. The cross-objective parameter comparison **RAN (2026-07-01)**: `ordinal::clmm` (Laplace-ML, probit — glmmTMB does NOT fit cumulative-link ordinal; MCMCglmm `threshold` Bayesian-agreement-only) on an identical A=I / repeated-records K=3 packet (80 animals × 4 records) agrees with `fit_laplace_reml(...; family=:ordered_probit)` — cutpoint SPACING Δ **0.004** (numerical proximity after aligning the intercept convention: engine `θ_2` == clmm `θ^c_2−θ^c_1`, engine β == `−θ^c_1`), σ²a Δ 0.024 (the cause of the difference is unestablished), intercept Δ 0.012, both converged (`docs/dev-log/recovery-checkpoints/2026-07-01-ordinal-clmm-comparator.md`, `comparator/ordinal_clmm/`). docs/design/validation-debt-register.md:110:| V6-NS-H2 | Non-Gaussian latent- and observation-scale heritability (Nakagawa–Schielzeth / de Villemereuil) (Phase 6, H7) | partial | `nongaussian_heritability(fit; mu, n_trials, predictor_variance)` + `nongaussian_heritability(sigma_a2, mu, family::ResponseFamily; predictor_variance)` (EXPORTED) compute the latent/link-scale h² = V_A/(V_A + V_link + V_fixed) and the observation/data-scale h² — the NS (2017) / de Villemereuil (QGglmm) transform filling the gap the family-uniform `nongaussian_result_payload` leaves (it carries NO heritability). Logit (Bernoulli/Binomial): V_link = π²/3 exactly (latent closed form, rtol 1e-12); observation scale on the PROPORTION estimand via the module's existing 20-node Gauss–Hermite, `V_A,obs = Ψ²·V_A` (Ψ = E[p(1−p)]; by Stein's lemma the regression-of-mean-on-breeding-value variance, so 0 < h²_obs < 1), `V_P,obs = Var(p) + Ψ/n_trials`. CRITICAL CONVENTION: π²/3 is the LATENT residual and is NOT added to the observation-scale integration variance N(μ, V_A+V_fixed) (matching QGglmm `binom1.logit`; corrects an over-broad reading of the spec). Poisson (log): latent h² = NaN (DEGENERATE — no latent residual); count scale via the log-normal–Poisson closed form. Gamma (log): latent h² is NON-degenerate — V_link = ψ₁(shape) = trigamma(shape) = Var[log Y] (EXACT, doc-19 §3.1; NOT the ln(1+1/ν) lognormal/CV approx), h²_latent = V_A/(V_A + ψ₁(ν) + V_fixed) (`method = :gamma_trigamma_latent`); the Gamma observation/DATA scale is now computed — `h²_obs = V_A/[e^{V_pred}(1+1/ν)−1]` (NS-2017 multiplicative, EXACT μ-independent lognormal form; `Ψ=E[μ]`, `V_P,obs=Var(μ)+E[μ²/ν]`), VALIDATED vs QGglmm's custom Gamma-log model to ~5e-11 (`comparator/qgglmm_gamma_observed/`). Gaussian reduces to V_A/(V_A+σ²e) on both scales (machine precision). Threshold families (`:bernoulli_probit`, `:ordered_probit`): the LIABILITY scale (= the latent scale, V_link = 1; Dempster–Lerner 1950) `h²_liab = V_A/(V_A + 1 + V_fixed)` in `h2_latent` (independent of μ and the cutpoints, `method = :probit_liability`). The BINARY (`:bernoulli_probit`) observed-0/1 scale is computed via the QGglmm probit integration over `η~N(μ,V_A+V_fixed)` (`Ψ²V_A/[p̄(1−p̄)]`) — verified EQUAL to the Dempster–Lerner `z²/[p(1−p)]` and `< h²_liab`; the ORDINAL (K>2) per-category observed scale is now computed as the VECTOR `h2_observation_by_category` (`h²_k = Ψ_k²V_A/[p_k(1−p_k)]` per category indicator, over `η~N(μ,V_A+V_fixed)`; the scalar `h2_observation` stays NaN), VALIDATED to ≤3e-8 vs QGglmm `model=ordinal` (`comparator/qgglmm_ordinal_observed/`). Validated (`test/runtests.jl`): the ordinal per-category vector incl. the K=2→binary-observed reduction; the Gaussian reduction; the `_trigamma` closed forms (ψ₁(1)=π²/6, ψ₁(2)=π²/6−1, ψ₁(½)=π²/2) + recurrence + the Gamma latent closed form (μ-independent, V_fixed denominator, monotone-in-ν, shape guards); the probit/ordinal liability closed form incl. the exact K=2 ordinal→bernoulli-probit reduction + the V_fixed denominator; the binary observed = Dempster–Lerner cross-check (≈1e-6, obs < liab); the logit latent closed form; the logit observation-scale anchored against an INDEPENDENT 64-node quadrature of the same integrals (rtol 1e-3, 0<h²_obs<1); the Poisson degeneracy + closed form vs independent integration (rtol 1e-6); the Binomial n_trials information gradient (h²_obs rises 1→5→20); and guards (refuses a non-converged fit; per-record varying n_trials → NaN+caveat; ambiguous μ on a multi-β fit throws; Bernoulli information_limited = true; unsupported families throw). Dependency-free (reuses the 20-node GH). NOT added to `nongaussian_result_payload`. Still needs — a same-estimand external comparator: QGglmm RUN + AGREES (≤4.5e-6, 25 comparisons) for the logit + binary-probit + Poisson(count) + Binomial(n>1) observation scales (all four QGglmm builtins; `comparator/qgglmm_probit_observed/`; doc-19 §5), the ordinal-K>2 observed comparator is now RUN + AGREES (≤3e-8 via QGglmm `model=ordinal`), and the Gamma-data observation scale (~5e-11 vs QGglmm's custom Gamma model; `comparator/qgglmm_gamma_observed/`); still owed an MCMCglmm comparator; a Fisher/Falconer review of the exact decomposition; single-trial Bernoulli error characterization, then assess whether correction is warranted; per-record / multivariate data-scale h²; beta-binomial / negative-binomial families; intervals/SEs; and an R-facing surface. docs/design/validation-debt-register.md:113:| V6-GGLLVM-LAPLACE | Genetic-GLLVM integrated-Laplace fitting — estimate the latent G_lat (Phase 6, #50 slice 3) | partial | `fit_gllvm_laplace_reml(Y, Ainv, family; rank, X)` (internal) ESTIMATES the rank-`K` latent loadings `Λ` (`G_lat = ΛΛ'`) by maximizing the K-factor fixed-and-genetic-effect integrated Laplace objective (`gllvm_laplace_marginal_loglik`) over `vec(Λ)` (NelderMead). The marginal depends on `Λ` only through `G_lat = ΛΛ'`, so it is rotation-invariant; the result reports the rotation-INVARIANT `genetic_covariance` / `latent_structure` (never the raw `Λ̂`, an arbitrary point on the rotation manifold). Validated (`test/runtests.jl`): the `K=1, T=1` Poisson case reduces to the single-factor `fit_laplace_reml` (`σ²a = λ̂²`, rtol 2e-3); a multi-trait Poisson rank-1 fit converges and its optimum improves over the start (objective maximized); and the Gaussian optimum's marginal equals `_multivariate_reml_loglik` at the estimated `Λ̂Λ̂'` (`R0 = σ²e·I`, rtol 1e-7) — self-consistency of the reported `G_lat`. A `structure = :factor_analytic` option additionally estimates a per-trait specific genetic variance `Ψ > 0` (`G_lat = ΛΛ' + diag(Ψ)`, on the `log` scale, by augmenting the loadings to `[Λ | diag(√Ψ)]` and reusing the marginal unchanged); validated by the Gaussian self-consistency at `Ĝ = Λ̂Λ̂'+Ψ̂`, `communality < 1` (since `Ψ̂ > 0`), `FA loglik ≥ low-rank loglik` (FA nests low-rank), a converging Poisson FA fit, and length/structure guards. The nested witness is an objective evaluation at L=0, not a successful FA optimization claim.
    65	
    66	All tau/2 comparisons above use loglik units because tau is defined in criterion units. Both candidate ranks must be eligible to select a rank. If either fails after its budget, return `selection_status=unavailable`, no selected rank/fit, a reason and all attempts. A sole successful candidate does not win by default. The user may request an explicit fixed rank independently; no silent fallback fit is made.
    67	
    68	Near-floor candidates can remain eligible under the experimental score, with `boundary_sensitive=true`. The floor flag is defined for both candidates because both now share c. It is not a claim of uniqueness identification. At or numerically below the bound is an admissibility failure. The fixed absolute floor is unit-dependent; no silent standardization, rescaling or new preprocessing is introduced. Unit-change validation must identify where selection changes because constraints change.
    69	
    70	## Returned object and future bridge
    71	
    72	Return `selected_fit` alongside plain selection metadata:
    73	
    74	| Field | Required meaning |
    75	| --- | --- |
    76	| selection_status, reason | selected, unavailable or unsupported_input, with a clear explanation. |
    77	| requested_ranks, selected_rank | Always requested {0,1}; selected integer or missing. |
    78	| criterion, criterion_status, q, penalties | reml_aic_covariance, experimental; per-candidate counts and scores. |
    79	| criterion_difference, tie_tolerance, near_tie | D=C1-C0, tau and numerical tie flag. |
    80	| records/design/relationship fingerprint | Demonstrate identical model inputs across candidates. |
    81	| candidate_summary | One row per requested rank, including unattempted/failed ranks and eligibility reason. |
    82	| attempts | One row per start/retry, preserving failures and diagnostic fields. |
    83	| boundary_sensitive, start_sensitive | Visible flags derived from retained fits and attempts. |
    84	| uncertainty_scope | conditional_on_selected_rank; no selection-adjusted uncertainty claim. |
    85	
    86	Each attempt row records rank, structure, start ID, retry index, attempted status, failure reason, converged, optimizer status/iterations, finite-value/PD checks, returned and reevaluated loglik, q/criterion when defined, per-trait uniqueness and floor distances, near-floor flags, eligibility and selected marker. Failed values are missing with reasons, never zero. The candidate summary separates the chosen within-rank start from the selected rank.
    87	
    88	The candidate_summary is the authoritative retained row for every requested rank, including preflight-unattempted ranks. The attempts table contains actual starts only; no synthetic optimizer-start rows are created for unattempted ranks. Preflight refusals mark both candidate-summary rows unattempted with the reason. Interrupts abort promptly and propagate cancellation; the future wrapper/harness must retain its partial attempt ledger and mark interrupted/unattempted rows without pretending to return a completed selection. The interruption mechanism is an implementation acceptance item, not permission to swallow an interrupt.
    89	
    90	Proposed function name `select_fa_rank` is reserved for design discussion. It is not an implemented export or approved R grammar. Any future R expert-control payload must preserve the full table, missing reasons, scores, flags and selected covariance/EBVs in original label order. The existing bounded R fixed-rank transport is verified at immutable R merge `e82f5c95`; automatic-selection fields are new work. [User-contract review](../dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/user-contract.md).
    91	
    92	Suggested summary: “This rule preferred zero shared genetic factors (diagonal genetic covariance) / one shared genetic factor among the two eligible candidates. The attempt table shows the comparison and any boundary or start sensitivity. Uncertainty from the fitted model is conditional on this chosen rank.” Avoid describing K as the true number of biological dimensions.
    93	
    94	## Freeze and remaining implementation obligations
    95	
    96	The candidate set, model shape, experimental score/parameter convention, signed difference, tie rule, strict two-candidate eligibility, retry ceiling and returned semantics are frozen for this bounded implementation proposal. The numerical acceptance tolerances above are predeclared engineering checks, not measured successes.
    97	
    98	The internal diagonal floor, actual retry initializer, numerical kernel-identification screen and interruption transport must be implemented and independently checked before running selection fits. They are specified acceptance obligations with clear failure outcomes, not current capabilities. Broader statistical selection performance, defaults and public promotion require the separate validation plan. No source/test, capability, validation-debt or release change is made here.
     1	# Experimental automatic genetic FA rank selection
     2	
     3	Status: implementation under verification. Julia focused and full package checks pass. R focused, required live and full package checks also pass. Independent source review and final programme acceptance remain pending. Public covered count remains seven.
     4	
     5	This comparison asks whether four traits are better described by separate genetic variances or by those variances plus one shared genetic factor. It compares K0 and K1 on the same observations. K0 still estimates a genetic variance for each trait. K counts shared factors; positive uniqueness variances keep the full genetic covariance matrix of full rank.
     6	
     7	The supported input is complete four-trait Gaussian data, a pedigree, an intercept for each trait, and one observation per observed animal. Both candidates estimate an unstructured residual covariance. Missing responses, repeated observations, other trait counts, other fixed effects and genomic/custom relationships are outside this route.
     8	
     9	## Julia
    10	
    11	```julia
    12	selection = select_fa_rank(Y, X, Z, pedigree; ids=pedigree.ids,
    13	                         traits=["t1", "t2", "t3", "t4"])
    14	selection.selection_status
    15	selection.candidate_summary
    16	selection.attempts
    17	selection.selected_fit
    18	```
    19	
    20	The experimental `reml_aic_covariance` score is minus twice the restricted log likelihood plus twice the nominal covariance parameter count. K0 has 14 parameters and K1 has 18. The reported difference is K1 minus K0, so a negative difference favors K1. Differences within 1e-6 are numerical ties and choose K0.
    21	
    22	Both candidates need an eligible converged fit. If either lacks one after the bounded start budget, selection is unavailable and there is no selected fit. Genetic and residual covariance must also be distinguishable after removing the trait intercepts. An identity relationship matrix and the stated all-half-sib design are refusal cases.
    23	
    24	## R
    25	
    26	Point `HSQUARED_JULIA_PROJECT` at the matching Julia checkout, then use the explicit expert control:
    27	
    28	```r
    29	selection <- hsquared(
    30	  cbind(t1, t2, t3, t4) ~ animal(1 | id, pedigree = ped),
    31	  data = dat,
    32	  control = hs_control(
    33	    engine = "julia",
    34	    engine_control = list(target = "multivariate", rank_selection = "auto")
    35	  )
    36	)
    37	print(selection)
    38	fit_diagnostics(selection)
    39	selection$candidate_summary
    40	selection$attempts
    41	fit <- selection$selected_fit
    42	```
    43	
    44	When selection succeeds, `fit` is an ordinary `hsquared_fit` and its existing extractors apply. When selection is unavailable, it is NULL. Omitted rank alone never requests automatic selection, and explicit rank, genetic structure or initialization cannot be combined with this control.
    45	
    46	The default iteration budget is 2000. In the retained eight-animal execution witness, both ranks were unavailable at that budget because all three starts were unconverged. The same ordinary starts converged at 10000 iterations and selected K0. Increasing the budget can help a particular fit; it does not guarantee convergence or reliable rank selection. Use `iterations = 10000` in Julia, or add it to R's `engine_control`, when inspecting that retained fixture.
    47	
    48	## Reading the result
    49	
    50	Both candidate-summary rows remain visible, including refused or unattempted candidates. The attempt table retains actual optimizer starts and their failure reasons. Its `optimizer_objective` column stores the raw negative log likelihood reported by the optimizer for troubleshooting. The comparison fields `loglik` and `criterion` are populated only after the independent same-covariance check passes; rejected or unfinished scores remain missing. The independently reevaluated likelihood and discrepancy can remain visible on a rejected attempt as diagnostics. Candidate ranges, covariance disagreement and start sensitivity use completed, verified attempts, including verified attempts that did not converge. Cancellation propagates and retains a partial ledger with no completed winner.
    51	
    52	In R, a propagated cancellation condition has class `hsquared_fa_rank_interrupt`. Its `partial_ledger` contains the candidate-summary and actual-attempt tables captured before interruption. Unfinished likelihood, iteration and convergence fields stay missing. It is an interrupted record, with no selected fit.
    53	
    54	The uniqueness floor is 1e-4 in each trait's squared units, so changes in trait units can affect the admissible candidates. Near-floor and start-sensitivity flags are visible. The score is an experimental comparison rule for this singular covariance family. It does not give a probability that a biological rank is true. Fit uncertainty is conditional on the selected rank; selection reliability and selection-adjusted interval coverage require separate evidence.
    55	
    56	The retained ordinary optimizer fixtures select K0. Selected-K1 fit construction and R transport have controlled witnesses built around eligible K1 fits; an ordinary optimizer-driven K1 selection has not been demonstrated. This execution gap is distinct from rank-recovery or reliability studies, which remain separate work.
